articles.title: Teenage girl allegedly raped in ‘heinous’ attack at Queensland residential care home
articles.excerpt:
State’s child safety minister Amanda Camm confirms police are investigating alleged attack west of Brisbane

A Queensland teenager has allegedly been raped in a state-funded residential care home in w...
articles.body_text:
State’s child safety minister Amanda Camm confirms police are investigating alleged attack west of Brisbane

A Queensland teenager has allegedly been raped in a state-funded residential care home in what has been described as a “heinous” act.

A staff member is accused of assaulting the girl, who is understood to be intellectually impaired, at the home west of Brisbane.

Queensland’s child safety minister, Amanda Camm, confirmed the alleged attack was being investigated and said she had zero tolerance for abuse, “particularly when it comes to vulnerable children in care”.

“Queenslanders would rightly expect that anyone convicted of such [an allegedly] heinous offence deserves to face the full force of the law,” she told reporters on Wednesday.

Detectives have been investigating the alleged 20 August assault at the home.

The out-of-home residential care provider, which serves vulnerable children and young people, has been contacted for comment.

The acting deputy police commissioner Rhys Wildman confirmed an investigation was under way, but declined to provide further detail, citing the alleged victim’s vulnerability.

Pressure about the child safety system has been mounting on Camm, after the Liberal National party government claimed it was “broken” before it came into power.

Camm said a commission of inquiry in June found about 67% of reported sexual exploitation in state care involved children in residential care.

“Sixty-seven per cent of children in residential care that have reported sexual abuse allegations is unacceptable,” she said, adding the government did “not have a moment to waste” in reforming the system.

Camm said contracts had been cancelled where residential care providers failed to meet safety and quality standards, and that such providers “have no place” in the system.

The government also responded to 52 recommendations made in the child safety inquiry’s final report, accepting 32 of them while committing $200m to implement them within 30 months.

The 11-month inquiry’s report exposed years of systemic failure, revealing no child had been adopted from state care since 2019.

The government has also been looking to establish an agency aimed at improving the protection of children from sexual abuse.

The attorney general, Deb Frecklington, said a bill to establish the Queensland Protection Commission would be introduced to parliament on Wednesday, with the hope of having it launch in early 2027.

The commission would be a “nation-leading” safeguarding agency for children and vulnerable people, bringing key child protection checks and safeguards under one roof, Frecklington said.

“It is vitally important that we set up an agency … so we can push back on predators to make sure that Queensland children are kept very safe.”

It came after a Child Death Review Board report found there were multiple opportunities missed to stop one of Australia’s most notorious paedophiles, Ashley Paul Griffith.

articles.title: Antisemitism royal commission ends hearings but delays report to avoid ‘distraction’ from Bondi anniversary
articles.excerpt:
Commissioner Virginia Bell resists push to extend antisemitism inquiry noting need for timely recommendations

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free...
articles.body_text:
Commissioner Virginia Bell resists push to extend antisemitism inquiry noting need for timely recommendations

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Commissioner Virginia Bell says she will delay – by four days – handing down her final report into antisemitism and social cohesion, in order not to distract from commemorations of the Bondi terror attack.

On Wednesday, the last day of public hearings of the royal commission, Bell resisted a public push to extend the commission’s work.

Bell said the letters patent for the royal commission stated her final report should be handed to government no later than 14 December 2027, the first anniversary of the Bondi terror attack.

She said she had noted the push, including from Jewish community leaders and parliamentarians, to extend the timeframe of her commission by some months in order to hear from more witnesses.

However she said the commission had worked hard to address all of its terms of reference “in accordance with that timetable, and I do not seek any meaningful extension of it”.

“Among other considerations, I note the evidence that has been given by senior public officials that the implementation of important policy proposals is awaiting the recommendations of this Commission.”

The commissioner added that she did not want the release of the report to distract from commemorations of the Bondi terror attack.

“The 14th of December is the anniversary of the massacre. It will be a solemn occasion marked by memorials. I’m aware of concern within the Jewish community that delivery of the report on the anniversary would be a distraction.

“I fully understand that concern and to avoid that distraction I have asked for a short extension of the term with a view to the submission of my final report on Friday the 18th of December.”

There has been significant pressure to extend the commission’s hearings.

Liberal MP Julian Leeser, who is Jewish, put an unsuccessful motion to parliament on 18 August for the reporting date to be extended “to allow the commission to hear and test evidence from key witnesses and properly investigate the individuals and institutions responsible”.

“Many significant Australian voices will have been left unheard and critical players not put on the stand,” he said.

“Australians are entitled to know how antisemitism spiralled so badly, who was responsible and what must change to ensure that it can never happen again. A royal commission cannot fully answer those questions if key people are never required to account for their actions.”

Senior security leaders, including a former governor general and retired heads of Australia’s military, signed an open letter, published on Wednesday, calling for the commission to be extended.

“The speed with which the royal commission has been forced to conduct its hearings has not allowed detailed review of the rise of antisemitism, Islamist and other forms of extremism in Australia,” the letter said.

Signatories include former governor general David Hurley, former chiefs of the army Peter Leahy and Rick Burr, and former heads of the Australian Secret Intelligence Service Paul Symon and Rex Stevenson.

Opening the final day of public hearings in Sydney, counsel assisting the commission Richard Lancaster SC, said that because of the ongoing criminal prosecution of one of the alleged Bondi terrorists, and the sensitivity of national security information, significant portions of the inquiry have had to take place in camera.

“A consequence is that those who are following the hearings of the commission would see only part of the story,” he said.

“The public record is not a complete picture of the work of the commission at the moment, and [public] commentary is necessarily made without an appreciation of the full scope of evidence and material that is available to you, commissioner, and that informs the work of counsel and solicitors assisting.”

On Sunday, 14 December 2025, two gunmen, alleged to have been inspired by Islamic State, opened fire on Jewish Australians celebrating Chanukah at Bondi Beach, killing 15 people.

articles.title: Dozens killed in rebel attacks on Sudan’s Kordofan, medical group says
articles.excerpt: A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kord...
articles.body_text:
A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kordofan.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sudan Doctors Network said the killings were carried out by the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas inhabited by the Otoro tribe in South Kordofan.

“The attacks resulted in a large wave of displacement among citizens towards the Abu Hitan area and Kadugli,” it said.

Targeting unarmed civilians on ethnic grounds constitutes a “clear violation of international humanitarian law”, the group added, warning that continued violations threatened to turn “the conflict in South Kordofan into a broader ethnic conflict”.

The killings follow intense fighting earlier this year between forces linked to SPLM-N and the Otoro tribe, which is a minority group in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan.

The ethnic standoff, first instigated by land disputes, adds another layer to the country’s ongoing civil war, which broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese army and the RSF.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country’s population, require humanitarian assistance.

articles.title: Instagram chief testifies at Meta trial, says few teens used safety feature
articles.excerpt: The top executive at Instagram has admitted that few teenagers have used a feature meant to counter addiction before it was turned on by default, as hearings in a landmark trial against its parent com...
articles.body_text:
The top executive at Instagram has admitted that few teenagers have used a feature meant to counter addiction before it was turned on by default, as hearings in a landmark trial against its parent company, Meta, continue in the United States.

Adam Mosseri testified on Tuesday as Meta’s trial – over accusations that it designed its platforms, including Facebook, to be addictive to young people – entered its second week.

Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, denied any suggestion by US states suing Meta that Instagram had stalled by not making the “Take a Break” feature the default setting for teenagers until September 2024, nearly three years after its launch.

“Most teens didn’t want it,” Mosseri said. “We decided to push forward with it anyway.”

Mosseri is a central witness in the lawsuit brought by 29 US states, in what experts call the biggest legal test yet of social media’s effects on young users.

Four of the states – California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey – have accused Meta of designing the platforms to hook young users, driving anxiety, depression and even suicide, while misleading consumers about the platforms’ safety.

All 29 states say Meta violated US federal law by improperly collecting and employing the personal data of children under 13 while they used its platforms.

The states are seeking approximately $200bn in damages from Meta.

Meta has rejected accusations that it sought to addict children, saying its research showed no clear link between adolescents’ social media use and a lack of wellbeing.

Under questioning from Jason Slothouber, a lawyer for Colorado, Mosseri acknowledged that the percentage of teenagers using Take a Break was in the low single digits before Instagram made it ⁠the default.

Take a Break encourages teenage users to close the app after a certain amount of time. Mosseri had estimated in a December 2021 blog post that more than 90 percent of teenagers who turned the feature on kept it on.

That number, however, referred to the number of those who had turned on the feature.

When asked whether Meta had disclosed its low adoption, which had reached only 1 or 2 percent of accounts, Mosseri admitted the company had not, but said the safety features were later turned on by default in Teen Accounts, which launched in 2024 and have parental controls.

Former Meta employees have said that features such as Take a Break and Quiet Mode were difficult to find and not widely used, casting doubt on whether they represented a serious effort by the company to limit screen time for young users.

“In my experience, Take a Break is a feature that’s designed to fail,” Arturo Bejar, a former Meta engineering director, testified last week.

George Volichenko, a data scientist who worked on safety features at Instagram in 2022 and 2023, likewise stated on Monday that adoption rates of such features were “very low” and that company leadership had declined to approve turning on Quiet Mode by default for young teenagers.

He added that turning on such features automatically would have had a “notable negative impact” on user engagement.

Jurors are expected to issue an advisory verdict. US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers will decide whether Meta is liable and, if so, determine any civil penalties and changes to Facebook and Instagram.

articles.title: NYC manhunt underway for suspect accused of deadly shootings across 2 boroughs days apart
articles.excerpt:
Police say Jesus Acosta is wanted in connection with two deadly shootings in Brooklyn and the Bronx.(Credit: FOX 5 New York)

A man accused of gunning down a customer during a Bronx deli robbery is al...
articles.body_text:
Police say Jesus Acosta is wanted in connection with two deadly shootings in Brooklyn and the Bronx.(Credit: FOX 5 New York)

A man accused of gunning down a customer during a Bronx deli robbery is also wanted in connection with a deadly Brooklyn shooting two days earlier, police said.

The suspect, identified by the NYPD as 31-year-old Jesus Acosta, is being hunted in connection with two deadly shootings that unfolded days apart across New York City, police told Fox News Digital.

The latest attack happened around 12:16 a.m. Tuesday at 149 Grill & Deli at 143 East 149th Street in the Bronx, where a gunman approached a 33-year-old man and opened fire, striking him multiple times in the chest, according to police and FOX 5 New York.

NEW YORK BODEGA WORKER KILLED LESS THAN A YEAR AFTER EXPRESSING FEAR TO REPORTER OVER VIOLENCE

The suspect, identified by the NYPD as 31-year-old Jesus Acosta, is being sought in connection with the two shootings that unfolded days apart in Brooklyn and the Bronx. (@NYPDnews via X)

After the shooting, the gunman forcibly removed an unknown amount of cash from behind the register and fled, police said.

The victim was rushed to Lincoln Hospital and was initially listed in stable condition, but later died from his injuries Tuesday. Police subsequently deemed the case a homicide.

Acosta is also wanted in connection with a shooting inside 842 Rockaway Ave. in Brooklyn shortly after midnight Sunday that left a 44-year-old man dead and another man wounded, the NYPD said.

The New York Post identified the location as American Best Wings & Pizza.

MAN FACES MURDER CHARGE AFTER INNOCENT 12-YEAR-OLD IS KILLED IN BRONX STREET GUNFIRE

Surveillance image released by the NYPD shows a person sought in connection with a deadly Bronx deli robbery. (NYPD)

Officers responding to a 911 call about an assault in progress found the 44-year-old victim with a gunshot wound to the head and a 39-year-old man suffering from a gunshot wound to the leg.

Both men were taken to One Brooklyn Health-Brookdale Hospital Medical Center, where the 44-year-old was pronounced dead. The 39-year-old man was listed in stable condition, according to police.

"Have you seen Jesus Acosta? He is wanted for the fatal shooting of a 44-year-old man on 8/23 inside 842 Rockaway Ave in Brooklyn and a robbery from 8/25 at 143 East 149 St in the Bronx," the NYPD wrote on X before announcing that the Bronx victim had also died.

Acosta is described as 5 feet, 11 inches tall and weighing about 175 pounds, with short brown hair and brown eyes.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY AFTER MASKED GUNMAN ALLEGEDLY SHOOTS NYC CAB DRIVER IN FACE DURING OVERNIGHT ROBBERY

The NYPD released surveillance images while seeking the public’s help locating Jesus Acosta. (NYPD)

He has the word "Bronx" tattooed on his hand and the name "Bobby" tattooed on his left forearm, the NYPD told Fox News Digital.

Police released surveillance images of Acosta and are urging anyone who recognizes him to come forward.

Sophia Compton is a Writer at Fox News Digital. Sophia was previously a business reporter covering finance, energy and tourism and has experience as a TV news producer. She graduated with a journalism degree in 2021 from the University of Hawaii at Manoa. Story tips can be sent to sophia.compton@fox.com.

articles.title: Fears for ‘gregarious’ local celebrity Sammy the elephant seal in Victorian bird flu hotspot
articles.excerpt:
Seals and sea lions often communicate by touch and share spaces with wild birds, placing them at risk of infection from H5N1 virus

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our brea...
articles.body_text:
Seals and sea lions often communicate by touch and share spaces with wild birds, placing them at risk of infection from H5N1 virus

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Since H5 bird flu arrived in Portland, Victoria, the situation has been “pretty grim” with many dead and suffering birds on the beach, and the dilemma of how to dispose of the carcasses, according to local resident Lynn Murrell.

But since the first confirmed case in a fur seal on Sunday at Beachport, South Australia – a two-hour trip over the border – people have been worried for their local “pet seal”, known as Sammy.

“He’s a great tourist attraction. The locals love him. So, we’d hate to see him get the flu,” Murrell, the president of the Southwest Environment Alliance, a coalition of local environment groups, said.

The male southern elephant seal had “kind of adopted the town”, frequenting the foreshore and port, and sometimes the community gardens. In recent weeks, the seal has been spotted near birds presumed to have died from H5N1.

Victoria’s first bird flu case was detected in the town, in the far south-west of the state, at the end of July. Since then, the area has become a hotspot, with 17 confirmed events in crested terns, magpies, silver gulls and ravens, according to the federal agriculture department, and many more suspected cases.

People were concerned about the carcasses, and the risk of the virus spreading as a result of scavengers eating them. Some have estimated 30 to 40 new sick and dying birds on the beach a day.

A spokesperson for Glenelg shire council said the situation was distressing for many in the community. They said the state government’s advice was to leave the dead birds in place, although council had begun removing some where “unacceptable public amenity or safety risks have been identified”.

Prof Rob Harcourt, at Macquarie University, said elephant seals like Sammy were “characters” and “the most gregarious animals you’ve ever seen”, which explained why communities named them.

Along with Sammy, a regular visitor to Portland, and Neil in Tasmania, many others had gained notoriety, including Humphrey, a three-tonne celebrity who frequented New Zealand coastal towns in the 1980s.

Southern elephant seals breed in large colonies, especially on Macquarie Island, Harcourt said. But because they’re so large and need a lot of food, they disperse widely to feed, migrating over 1,000 kilometres.

They’re strong swimmers, but on land they “move along like caterpillars,” he said.

Seals and sea lions often share spaces with wild birds, placing them at risk of infection from H5 bird flu. In Victoria, more than 100 marine mammals have been reported to the emergency animal disease hotline this month, although none so far have been confirmed as positive cases.

Seals were also vulnerable because they’re “thigmotactic”, Harcourt said, which means they love to lie touching each other. They recognised one another through “nasal exchange”. “They sniff each other’s faces”, he said; “mothers recognise their pups by touching noses”.

Southern elephant seals, listed as vulnerable under federal environment laws, were at “very high risk” of H5 bird flu, according to a national assessment. The deadly strain killed more than 13,000 pups on Heard Island in 2025 and 2026.

Australian sea lions, listed as endangered, were a particular concern given their low numbers. “Sea lions are like the labradors of the sea. They’re friendly and playful, and they’re curious,” Harcourt said. “I will be totally and utterly devastated if we lose them.”

With so many birds suffering, volunteer wildlife carers from western Victoria travelled to Portland last weekend, in a bid to humanely euthanise birds, which were being left to die slow, painful deaths.

“This is a Band-Aid over a bleeding wound,” David Mould from the Victorian Wildlife Alliance said. “This is not a solution. This is a couple of volunteers picking up the slack of what should be a major government operation.”

“The decline is rapid. These birds can’t fly. They have neurological symptoms,” he said. “They lose their ability to walk, and they start staggering around having seizures. You see them with their wings splayed out to support them off the ground, until they lose even the strength to do that.”

articles.title: Nine CEO confident new AI laws will deliver a ‘world of growth in publishing’ as network slashes costs
articles.excerpt:
Matt Stanton says company has ‘good pipeline’ of AI deals ahead even as it aims to cut $160m in costs

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or ...
articles.body_text:
Matt Stanton says company has ‘good pipeline’ of AI deals ahead even as it aims to cut $160m in costs

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The head of Nine Entertainment sees a “world of growth in publishing” on the horizon backed by laws designed to force tech platforms into commercial deals, even as the network cuts costs across its newsrooms.

Parliament passed revamped media bargaining laws last week, clearing the way for levies on global tech platforms that fail to strike deals with Australian news outlets for the use of their journalism.

Nine’s chief executive officer, Matt Stanton, told analysts on Wednesday he expected platforms such as Google and Facebook owner Meta to contribute amounts comparable to those under their previous arrangement, struck in 2021.

“There’s a number of variables that fly around, not just in news media bargaining, but yes, there is a world of growth in publishing,” Stanton said.

He said Nine also had a “good pipeline” of AI deals coming through after recently signing an agreement allowing Microsoft’s Copilot to access content.

The upbeat outlook comes at a challenging time for the broadcaster and publisher, which is stripping out more than $160m in costs over a three-year period as it revamps its business.

Nine recently announced a redundancy program at its Sydney Morning Herald and the Age newsrooms after the metropolitan mastheads were hit by a prolonged, weak advertising market.

Nine’s business masthead, the Australian Financial Review, has been spared the cuts and remains a robust revenue earner, according to financial results for the year to 30 June released on Wednesday.

Nine reported broadly flat revenue streams from its publishing arm, and a small decline from its streaming and broadcast unit, despite a record result for Stan. Nine’s television network has been weighed down by a weak advertising market.

Stanton said the company was focusing on “growth assets”, which include its newly acquired digital outdoor media company QMS, while it reduces exposure to “structurally challenged and smaller assets”.

Nine recorded a full-year net profit result of $142m from continuing businesses.

articles.title: Trump-endorsed candidate clears key hurdle in red state gubernatorial race
articles.excerpt: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secures a significant victory over incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary runoff, fueled by President Donald Trump's endorsement. Political strategis...
articles.body_text:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secures a significant victory over incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary runoff, fueled by President Donald Trump's endorsement. Political strategist Cassie Smedile emphasizes the enduring power of Trump's support among the Republican base. Paxton is now preparing to challenge Democratic candidate James Talarico in the general election, highlighting the contentious political landscape in Texas.

Mike Mazzei, a former Oklahoma state senator and financial planner, won a primary election runoff on Tuesday evening with the backing of President Donald Trump to secure the GOP nomination for governor in Oklahoma.

Having beaten out Genter Drummond, the current Oklahoma attorney general, Mazzei is now the heavy favorite to become the Sooner State’s next governor. His win is also a political victory for outgoing Gov. Kevin Stitt, who has opposed Drummond for years.

Stitt and Drummond have sparred over lawsuits, pointed letters and public criticisms. At one point, Stitt even described Drummond as a "longtime political enemy" in a quote to local outlets.

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SPARKS RUNOFF AGAINST POPULAR PROSECUTOR IN KEY GUBERNATORIAL RACE

Gov. Kevin Stitt, R-Okla., (left) and Oklahoma Attorney General Genter Drummond disagree on whether the First Amendment allows the Oklahoma Statewide Charter School Board to grant St. Isidore of Seville Catholic Charter School public funding. (Getty/AP)

The feud between them centers on Drummond’s attacks of Oklahoma poultry companies for what he sees as decades of phosphorus pollution in water supplies. Stitt has rebuffed those characterizations, calling them an overreach of Drummond’s role as attorney general and warning that litigation against the companies could threaten jobs and the agricultural industry of the state.

Stitt endorsed Mazzei, stating that "we want a pro-business governor in there to take the lead for the next four years."

Stitt is prevented by term limits from running again. His exit prompted a crowded field of hopefuls to replace him, but after an initial primary on June 2, no candidate secured the 50% support needed to lock up the nomination outright.

Only Drummond and Mazzei advanced to a runoff.

Like Stitt, President Donald Trump also endorsed Mazzei, calling him a "MAGA warrior."

"As a successful Businessman, and former Chairman of the State Senate Finance Committee, and later, as Oklahoma’s Secretary of Budget, Mike knows the AMERICA FIRST Policies required to Grow our Economy, Create GREAT Jobs, Cut Taxes and Regulations, Promote MADE IN THE U.S.A., and Unleash American Energy DOMINANCE," Trump wrote in a May post to Truth Social.

TRUMP-BACKED FIREBRAND WINS ARIZONA GOP GOVERNOR PRIMARY, SETTING UP HIGH-STAKES SHOWDOWN

President Donald Trump speaks during an event in the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington, D.C., on Monday, Aug. 24, 2026. Trump hosted the Rose Garden event to celebrate the administration's efforts on school choice. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Mazzei based his campaign on promises to cut taxes, among other state-government reforms.

"I have a detailed plan to eliminate Oklahoma’s income tax in six years. I have a plan to eliminate property taxes for seniors and veterans," Mazzei said in a campaign video posted to Instagram.

In addition to tax reforms, Mazzei highlighted preventing foreign nationals from buying up state land, bolstering the Oklahoma education system and government spending accountability.

In turn, Mazzei tried to paint Drummond as a fake Republican with a penchant for expanding government.

"His solution to every problem is to raise taxes and grow government," Mazzei said.

"He doesn’t understand money and finance. Crunching numbers is a skill you pick up when you earn your wealth rather than inherit it."

In his own campaign, Drummond, a multigenerational rancher and former fighter pilot, highlighted his record as attorney general. On his website, he touted having confronted Chinese criminal operations growing illegal marijuana farms, shutting down thousands of their illegal grow operations and enforcing immigration law.

"As a tough-on-crime attorney general and decorated fighter pilot, I have proven I will always fight for our freedom and defend our values," Drummond said in a campaign video.

TRUMP SWITCHES SUPPORT IN OKLAHOMA CONGRESSIONAL RACE AS FORMERLY ENDORSED PASTOR CANDIDATE SUSPENDS CAMPAIGN

Oklahoma state lawmaker Mike Mazzei gestures to reporters. (Nathan Fish/IMAGN)

"I’ll keep standing strong with President Trump to secure the border, deport illegals and stop the flow of drugs and crime," Drummond said.

The Club for Growth, a pro-small-government group that advocates for lower taxes and free-market principles and contributed $9 million in support of Mazzei, praised his win.

"Mike Mazzei is a principled conservative who will advocate for lower taxes, fewer regulations, and for Oklahoma parents to have a voice in their children’s education," Club for Growth PAC President David McIntosh said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Meanwhile, Gentner Drummond has spent his career putting radical education bureaucrats ahead of families by opposing school freedom. The message is clear, if you oppose school freedom and call yourself a Republican, expect to lose your next primary."

Having cleared the primary, Mazzei will face off against Democratic nominee Cyndi Munson, House minority leader in the Oklahoma House of Representatives. The general election is set for Nov. 3.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

articles.body_text:
Newly obtained text messages from Dr. Anthony Fauci's device reveal private concerns about the safety of the COVID-19 vaccine during pregnancy, according to Sen. Ron Johnson. The documents contradict Fauci's public claims that the vaccine was safe and effective.

When Sen. Rand Paul released private texts and messages from Anthony Fauci to the public several weeks ago, it brought the now-former head of the National Institutes of Allergy and Infectious Diseases back into the national conversation.

Many involved in that national conversation have been critical of what the "Fauci diaries" revealed. That the supposedly unbiased "expert" was, in fact, anything but. Instead, he was an arrogant, self-obsessed, fame-hungry, frequently dishonest narcissist.

Other "news" outlets like CNN or MSNBC either ignored the controversy over his diary, and the many inconsistencies in it, preferring to avoid humiliating themselves for their past hero worship.

ANTHONY FAUCI DIARY ENTRIES SET SOCIAL MEDIA ABLAZE AS CRITICS MOCK, CONDEMN BEHAVIOR

It wasn't just the emails that caused embarrassment for Fauci and his media partners, however. Text messages released by Sen. Ron Johnson showed that he had legitimate concerns over the possibility that COVID vaccines were causing side effects in pregnant mothers. Concerns that warranted further investigation, regardless of the outcome.

Former NIH Director Anthony Fauci is sworn in before testifying to Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on July 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Well, there are some more new text messages that should cast doubt on both Fauci's public statements and the media's all-too-willing promotion of them.

One such message came from Michael Osterholm. Osterholm is an epidemiologist at the University of Minnesota, as well as a professor in the school's public health department. Importantly, he's also the director of the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy (CIDRAP). CIDRAP became famous during COVID when one of their articles, published in April 2020, acknowledged the truth, that there was no evidence to support cloth masking to stop the spread of the virus. They then were forced to issue "clarifications" when pressure became overwhelming to support masks, regardless of the data and evidence.

Osterholm sent this text message in August 2021 to several people, with just their first names included. One was "Jeff," likely Jeff Zients, the COVID response coordinator at the start of the Biden administration. Another was "Vivek," again likely Vivek Murthy, the Surgeon General under Biden. Then there was "Tony," the popular nickname for Fauci among those who knew him personally. And finally "Rochelle," which was almost certainly a reference to then-CDC director Rochelle Walensky.

The contents of the text were enormously revealing, as it confirmed what most Fauci-critics long suspected: they all knew the masks they'd been recommending didn't work.

FAUCI DISCUSSED COVID MRNA VACCINE CONCERNS FOR PREGNANT WOMEN IN TEXT CHAIN RELEASED BY SENATE COMMITTEE

Dr. Rochelle Walensky, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, testifies during a Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 11, 2022. (Shawn Thew-Pool/Getty Images)

"Dear Jeff, Vivek, Tony and Rochelle, I'm sending this via text messaging to avoid any FOIA issues," Osterholm started, in a clear admission that these "experts" frequently worked to hide information from the public.

"On Friday a Newsmax reporter asked Jen Psaki about my comments on face cloth coverings and protection against SARS-CoV-2 transmission. The reporter completely mischaracterized my comments made on numerous occasions over the past 16 months about 'masks' and the prevention of SARS-CoV-2 transmission. She was taking the Florida governor's approach. Since April, 2020, I have been consistent in my messaging about the roles that aerosols play in transmission, and the limited benefit that cloth face coverings play in reducing risk."

Ah, yes. The very cloth masks that Fauci, Walensky, Murthy and Zients had worked tirelessly to promote to the American people. The cloth masks that were mandated by politicians across the country, forced onto toddlers, those with learning disabilities, or with compliance requirements that resulted in disagreements, fights, or being removed from businesses or other public places. They didn't work, because the virus was transmitted via aerosols and not droplets. And the science on this was clear, and had not changed since April 2020.

ONE OF THE MOST PROMINENT PRO-MASK MANDATE STUDIES DURING THE COVID PANDEMIC WAS A MISLEADING FAILURE

Osterholm knew this, had clearly told the other "experts" the same, and they ignored the science and pushed masks anyway.

The text continues by acknowledging that the "national industrial hygienists expert group on respiratory protection" had found that cloth face coverings had virtually no protective benefit as opposed to wearing nothing.

"N-95s are necessary to be effective reducing risk with aerosol transmission. Here is a link to the ACGIH website (the national industrial hygienists expert group on respiratory protection.) (https://1lnfej4c7wie44voctzq1r57-wpengine.netdna-ssl.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Fact_Sheet_Face-Mask.pdf) Note the very limited protection from face cloth coverings versus no respiratory protection at all."

In order to save face with Fauci, Walensky and Murthy, Osterholm then adds that he supports "masking," but that it should be with N95 masks. That's also wrong, as we'll see shortly, but at the very least there's more rational basis for it than the masks Fauci and Walensky demanded people wear. More importantly though, Osterholm once again reveals the uncomfortable truth: all of the CDC's supporting "evidence" was essentially fake.

"CMS has supported an expert review group process for evaluating respiratory protection studies since the early days of the pandemic and have found none of the studies that CDC uses to support its statement as to the significant protection of face cloth coverings stand up to scientific scrutiny," he wrote.

Imagine if this had been widely reported and acknowledged in 2020 and 2021. The CDC's research on masks was virtually useless. Some, who, ahem, wrote books about this, had pointed that out at the time. But to see Osterholm tell Fauci and Walensky that the "studies" they used and referred to were garbage is both refreshing and infuriating.

Former NIH Director Anthony Fauci listens during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on July 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Fauci declined to answer questions, asserting his Fifth Amendment right. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

These are highly credentialed "experts" who know what high-quality research looks like. For all their flaws, they weren’t and aren’t unintelligent or uneducated. They knew that the CDC had put out junk science to justify their position on masks, then promoted and defended it anyway because they wanted mask mandates, even though those mandates were obviously failing.

Osterholm wasn't done there, saying that the CDC's mistakes didn't end there.

"As we all know, CDC was very late to the game recognizing that aerosols play a significant role in the transmission picture. Just look at the current US map of Delta activity and see how fast and far it has spread throughout the US. This is largely aerosol transmission driven, not respiratory droplets," Osterholm said.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Aerosols were the driving force of COVID transmission. Which meant that masks were always going to be useless, as pre-pandemic planning research had already confirmed. The CDC took an extraordinarily long time to admit that, likely because they knew what it meant about masking.

Osterholm goes on to urge more N95 masks, but closes with this important takeaway: "I am certain one day that one of the take-away findings of this pandemic was the constant USG emphasis on masking while at the same time providing minimal guidance to the public what effective masking means."

He was right, to an extent. There is no such thing as "effective masking." But the obsessive government emphasis on it was and is a constant, permanent source of embarrassment and failure. Masks didn't work, and public health officials torched their credibility to pretend they did.

Oh, and those N95 masks? Yeah they didn't work either. Several German states followed Osterholm's advice and mandated N95-grade masks in public. They then reported higher case rates than the states that had "lower quality" mandates.

Comparison of COVID case rates in German states with N95 mask mandates and those with surgical mask mandates (Ian Miller)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

None of it worked. And they all knew it and pretended otherwise anyway.
