articles.title: Typhoon Narra: record flood waters submerge homes and force mass evacuations in China
articles.excerpt:
Heavy rain expected in parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China, as another storm system, Typhoon Saudel, heads for Japan and Taiwan

Widespread flooding triggered by Typhoon Narra has submerged homes and...
articles.body_text:
Heavy rain expected in parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China, as another storm system, Typhoon Saudel, heads for Japan and Taiwan

Widespread flooding triggered by Typhoon Narra has submerged homes and forced mass evacuations in southern China, as another storm system tracked towards Japan and Taiwan.

Authorities in Chongzuo, in China’s Guangxi region – famous for its giant waterfalls and karst limestone mountains – on Tuesday evacuated more than 15,000 people after water ⁠levels surpassed a record high set in 2008.

Rising flood waters have prompted China to relocate a total of 54,000 people in Guangxi, state television said.

Narra made landfall as a tropical storm on Tuesday evening ⁠in China’s southern island province of Hainan after lingering over the Beibu Gulf for ‌several days, dumping heavy rain on ‌Guangxi, Hainan and Guangdong.

Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, state media said.

In Chongzuo, river water overflowed into the city, with water levels reaching the rooftops of some buildings and power lines.

A notice from Chongzuo authorities on Monday ordered all businesses and tourist operations to cease and urged evacuated residents not to return to high-risk areas.

Meanwhile, medium-strength Typhoon Saudel moved towards southern Japan and northern Taiwan where ‌it is expected to bring sporadic heavy rain, as Taiwan reported one dead and four missing from a separate weather system over its south and east.

Japan’s weather agency warned of destructive winds and high seas as Typhoon Saudel approached the south-western islands of Okinawa prefecture.

Saudel is expected to pass to the north of Taiwan starting late Thursday and into Friday, though its intensity is forecast to gradually weaken, the island’s Central Weather Administration said.

However, there is uncertainty about ⁠the timing and extent of the typhoon’s rainfall impact, it added.

In southern and eastern Taiwan, ​the government reported one person dead and ​four missing from a tropical depression ​that brought flooding in the cities of Tainan and Kaohsiung, home to more than 4 million people.

During ​the three days from ‌Sunday to Tuesday, almost ​a metre (3.9 feet) of ​rain fell in Kaohsiung, which the government said exceeded rainfall during 2009’s devastating Typhoon Morakot that killed about 700 people and caused damage of up to $3bn.

Saudel is forecast to hit the coast in the south-eastern Chinese province of Fujian from late Thursday to early Friday.

articles.title: Malaysia’s Anwar puts non-aligned stance in focus with remarks on Taiwan
articles.excerpt: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia – Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s recent comments about Taiwan have raised questions about whether Malaysia is still committed to its traditional policy of non-alignmen...
articles.body_text:
Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia – Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s recent comments about Taiwan have raised questions about whether Malaysia is still committed to its traditional policy of non-alignment and not picking sides between China and the United States.

In an interview with Al Jazeera that aired earlier this month, Anwar stated that he saw Taiwan “as part of China, period”, adding that this was “accepted by all”.

More controversially, when asked whether he would condemn China if it resorted to force in the event that peaceful “reunification” did not work, Anwar said that if a Malaysian state were attempting to break away, he would use force to “protect the sanctity and unity of” Malaysia.

Anwar’s comments were praised by the Chinese government, with a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman stressing that Taiwan is “an inalienable part of China’s territory” and that “China must and will be reunited”.

Taiwan’s government condemned the remarks and warned that Anwar’s “one-sided support for China could negatively impact Taiwanese businesses’ confidence in investing in Malaysia”.

Taiwan, the world’s largest chips producer, is a major investor in Malaysia, particularly in the country’s crucial semiconductor industry.

Asked about the issue by local media, Anwar appeared to walk back some of his comments, stressing that Malaysia respected China’s position but favoured a peaceful resolution to tensions in the Taiwan Strait.

Anwar courted headlines again several days after his Al Jazeera interview when he called for the bolstering of Malaysia’s defences in the Bornean state of Sabah.

He pointed to the development of US-backed military facilities in neighbouring Philippines as justification, in part, for increased defence spending.

The Philippine government is in the process of upgrading military facilities on the island of Balabac, 50km (31 miles) from the Malaysian islands of Banggi and Balambangan.

Balabac was recently added to the Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) between Washington and Manila, which granted US forces access to designated locations in the Philippines.

Anwar’s comments have bolstered longstanding suspicions among Western commentators that Malaysia is turning against the West and aligning with China, breaking from Malaysia’s traditional policy of non-alignment.

Indeed, Anwar’s remarks come amid China’s growing economic presence in Malaysia, with Beijing now representing Malaysia’s largest trade partner.

Malaysia has also been one of the most enthusiastic recipients of Chinese investment projects, including under China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

Anwar’s seemingly pro-China stance also comes as Malaysia diverges from the West on other geopolitical issues, such as the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

Long a firm critic of Israel, Malaysia under Anwar has been especially vocal in its opposition to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

However, some analysts push back against suggestions of Malaysia undergoing a strategic realignment.

Chee Meng Tan, an assistant professor of business economics at the University of Nottingham Malaysia, noted that Malaysia’s recognition of Taiwan as “part of China” dates to the 1974 communiqué that then-Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak signed with Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai to establish diplomatic relations between their countries.

“What was new was Anwar’s statement on the potential use of force, which the one China policy policy does not explicitly require,” Tan said.

Tan notes that Anwar’s comments should also be seen in the context of his upcoming trip to China in September, as he may be attempting to appease Beijing.

Daniel Loebell, a PhD student at Northwestern University in the US who has studied Chinese investments in Malaysia, suggested that Anwar’s position merely represents a realist understanding of territorial integrity.

“Though this idea of violence against Taiwan is immensely troubling to me, I do not think it differs from Malaysia’s policy at all, as he believes that the PRC attacking Taiwan would amount to attacking a rebel organisation within a single state’s own borders,” Loebell said, using the acronym for the People’s Republic of China.

“As head of the government, Anwar sees recognising one government of China amounting to the PRC government’s exclusive right to a monopoly on the use of force within its borders.”

Anwar’s later comments expressing unease over the US-backed base on Balabac can be viewed as linked to Malaysia’s ongoing dispute with the Philippines over the status of Sabah.

The Philippines has claimed Sabah since the territory joined Malaysia in 1963, a claim Malaysia has consistently rejected.

Manila would reaffirm its claim to Sabah in February this year, maintaining that the Philippines’ Maritime Zones Act 2024 preserved its “existing and valid claims” over part of the state.

In July, the Malaysian government lodged a formal protest with the United Nations over the Philippines’ claim to an extended continental shelf, which Malaysia argued encroached on Sabahan waters.

Tan, the assistant professor, argued that Anwar’s comment on the Balabac military buildup may be “a ‘protect-my-border’ reflex rather than a pro-China gesture”.

Anwar’s call to invest in Sabah’s defences also comes as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its defence posture in Borneo, largely to bolster its claims in the disputed South China Sea, where Malaysia is a claimant state alongside China.

While Malaysia has taken a decidedly less vocal stance on the South China Sea dispute than the Philippines, it has nonetheless maintained strong defence ties with Western powers, partly to quietly balance against China’s aggressive military buildup in the disputed waters.

This is demonstrated in Malaysia’s continued commitment to the Five Powers Defence Arrangements (FPDA), a multilateral security framework that also includes Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

While not a binding defence treaty, the FPDA commits its members to consult with one another in the event of an armed attack on Malaysia or Singapore. Under the framework, two major exercises are held annually – Bersama Shield and Bersama Lima – involving personnel and assets from member countries.

The FPDA maintains an air defence operations arm with headquarters at a Malaysian Air Force base in Butterworth, Penang, headed by a senior Australian Air Force officer.

Australia also maintains a rifle company at Butterworth and a regular maritime security presence in the region via the deployment of maritime patrol aircraft to Malaysia.

As a central pillar of the FPDA, Malaysia facilitates a Western military presence in the region, which analysts argue provides Malaysia with a quiet deterrent for would-be aggressors.

While Malaysia recognises the benefits of continued defence ties with the West, it also gains from continued Western investment.

As Loebell, the PhD student, noted, Malaysia has “maintained diverse economic relations with many states, and this has kept it from deeply aligning with any major power”.

“The USA still maintains as favourable an economic position as China does,” said Loebell, who doubts that Malaysia is seeking to align more closely with China.

“What’s more, Taiwan’s enterprises continue to invest heavily in Malaysia’s semiconductor industry, and Anwar undoubtedly knows and welcomes this.”

articles.title: Suburban Rail Loop: Victorian government secretly increased public transport fares to help pay for controversial SRL
articles.excerpt:
Labor put ‘levy on all public transport fares in metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria’ since January 2025, auditor general says

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our...
articles.body_text:
Labor put ‘levy on all public transport fares in metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria’ since January 2025, auditor general says

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian government secretly increased public transport fares to raise money to help pay for the Suburban Rail Loop and other Big Build projects, the state’s auditor general has revealed.

The auditor general’s report, tabled in parliament on Wednesday, also questioned whether the first stage of the multibillion-dollar project – a 26km stretch of twin tunnels from Cheltenham to Box Hill dubbed SRL East – can be delivered on time or within budget.

The auditor general found the plan to fund SRL East – via $11.5bn from both the commonwealth and state governments and $11.5bn through so-called value capture methods – “is not transparent and some funding sources are uncertain”.

It said in December, the government announced five value capture measures: using existing land tax and windfall gains tax revenue in SRL East precincts, infrastructure contributions from property developers, revenue from state-initiated property development and a car parking levy.

But the auditor general said the government did not reveal it had already introduced a levy on all public transport fares in metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria on 1 January 2025.

The levy involves a 1% annual increase on all public transport fares for nearly 40 years, on top of existing adjustments in line with inflation.

“The government plans to allocate 60% of the revenue it collects through the levy, estimated at $4.8bn in net present value (NPV) terms to 2062, to fund SRL East,” the report reads.

“This levy will be the project’s largest source of value capture revenue.

“The government and Transport Victoria did not acknowledge the levy in their public communications about the 2025 and 2026 annual fare increases. As at June 2026, they still have not announced it.”

Estimated cost of the entire the Suburban Rail Loop when announced by Daniel Andrews in 2018

Length of the loop, which would run from Cheltenham in Melbourne’s south-east to Werribee in the west, via Melbourne airport

Cost of stage one of the loop, dubbed SRL East, as promised by new premier Ben Carroll on 25 August 2026. It was estimated to cost $30-34.5bn in 2021

Worth of contracts signed, according to Labor’s May budget

Length of SRL East, which runs from Cheltenham to Box Hill

stimated cost of building SRL East and SRL North, the second stage of the project, based on a 2024 Parliamentary Budget Office analysis

Estimated cost of operating SRL East and North for 50 years, according to PBO

SRL North, which runs from Box Hill to Melbourne airport, due to open

Completion of SRL West, the final stage of project, running from Sunshine to Werribee

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, described the levy as a “secret public transport tax” and a “scandal of the highest order”.

“The independent auditor general has exposed that Labor has taxed every single public transport fare since January 2025 and they never told the public about it,” she said in a statement following the report’s release.

“What other secret taxes are Labor levying on Victorians without telling them?”

Wilson laid the blame on the new premier, Ben Carroll, who was public transport minister at the time the levy was approved in 2021.

The auditor general’s report said the work to find ways to generate $11.5bn through value capture began in April 2021 with support from the Department of Treasury and Finance (DTF). By August, DTF came back with a proposal that would raise about $6.5bn to 2062, which the report said “fell significantly short”.

“To address the funding shortfall the government agreed to introduce an additional ‘rail improvement charge’ on metropolitan heavy rail fares by no later than 2025,” it reads.

The report notes the levy is generating less revenue than forecast, due to policies such as making public transport free for children and free for seniors on weekends, free travel during the fuel crisis and half-price fares until the end of the year.

The auditor general said in April it received advice from DTF that public transport fare revenue for metropolitan Melbourne was about 20% under budget in the six months to 31 December 2025 and total revenue collected from the levy between January 2025 and the end of February 2026 was $6.2m – “significantly below the forecast revenue from this value capture measure over this period”.

The report also revealed the state government has approved budget funding of $23.3bn for the project but only publicly announced $11.8bn.

A funding gap of $5.5bn also remains because the federal government has committed “less to the project than has been assumed and requested by the state”.

The gap means the state “does not have sufficient funding approved to sign the contract for the second stations package”, the report said, which is contributing to “significant delays” putting at risk SRL East’s promised 2035 completion date.

It said the project is “more likely than not to exceed its publicly disclosed cost of up to $34.5bn”, due to costs related to “unexpected ground conditions and contamination”, “higher than expected market pricing” for the linewide and station contracts, and “added project costs and delays because of government decisions to slow down spending on the project to manage the state’s debt levels”.

In written responses to the auditor general report, the secretary of the Department of Transport and Planning, Jeroen Weimar, and Chris Barrett, the new Department of Premier and Cabinet secretary appointed by Carroll, denied the levy was a funding mechanism for the SRL. They both also maintained the project would be delivered on time and within budget.

The report comes a day after Carroll pledged to deliver $2bn in savings for SRL East.

articles.title: Surrogate, California couple clash in court as newborn fights for life after heart surgery
articles.excerpt:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton discusses a surrogate who gave birth in Texas to baby with a heart defect after the biological parents requested abortion on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

The critically ill...
articles.body_text:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton discusses a surrogate who gave birth in Texas to baby with a heart defect after the biological parents requested abortion on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

The critically ill newborn at the center of a bitter surrogate custody fight was placed back on a breathing tube after his condition worsened following open-heart surgery, according to newly filed court documents.

The baby is in critical condition and being closely watched at the hospital, intended parents Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed said in filings obtained by TMZ.

The couple said the child suffered possible complications after a Norwood procedure, an operation used to treat his severe heart defect, and had to be re-intubated after his condition declined overnight.

SURROGATE SAYS BABY 'RIPPED AWAY' 60 SECONDS AFTER BIRTH AS CUSTODY FIGHT ERUPTS AFTER ABORTION REFUSAL

McKenna West, center, walks with her legal team at a Dallas family court hearing in the legal fight over a critically ill newborn. (LM Otero/AP Photo)

In a Dallas courtroom Tuesday, Gilkar and Ahmed faced surrogate McKenna West as they fought over who should make medical decisions for the newborn. The clash has drawn national attention because West says she refused the California couple’s earlier request to terminate the pregnancy after the baby was diagnosed with a life-threatening heart condition.

Gilkar and Ahmed call the baby Rumi. West, an Alaska cardiac nurse, calls him Gabriel and is asking a Texas judge to give her sole conservatorship, which would put medical decision-making in her hands.

HHS WARNS TEXAS HOSPITALS AGAINST DENYING LIFE-SAVING CARE TO NEWBORN WITH DISABILITY

California couple Nausheen Gilkar, center, and Omar Ahmed, right, arrive for a hearing over custody and medical decision-making for their newborn son. (LM Otero/AP Photo)

Gilkar told the court the couple has been at their son’s bedside as he fights through treatment. She said that since surgery, he has struggled to breathe, choked on tubes and needed a blood transfusion, according to court reporting by The Associated Press.

"He’s our child," Gilkar said, according to the AP.

She accused West of trying to take him away. "She’s trying to take him from us," Gilkar said.

Gilkar described the newborn as "the love of our lives" and said, "He’s suffering a lot."

NEONATOLOGIST SOUNDS ALARM OVER MASSACHUSETTS ABORTION LAW ALLOWING PROCEDURES UP TO BIRTH: 'VERY DISTURBING'

McKenna West arrives at a Dallas court hearing over the custody dispute. (LM Otero/AP Photo)

The custody feud began after the baby was diagnosed at about 20 weeks with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, or HLHS. West says Gilkar and Ahmed then asked her to terminate the pregnancy. She refused and later traveled to Texas to give birth, Fox News Digital previously reported.

HLHS leaves one side of the heart underdeveloped and disrupts normal blood flow. Without treatment, the condition can be fatal within days or weeks, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

AMERICAN RED CROSS DECLARES NATIONAL BLOOD CRISIS AS TYPE O SUPPLY DROPS TO DANGEROUS LEVELS

McKenna West, left, appears with attorneys at Dallas family court amid a custody dispute with the intended parents of the baby she carried. (LM Otero/AP Photo)

Budner disputes key parts of West’s account and says the couple did agree to the baby’s treatment. He told Fox News Digital that doctors determined on Aug. 14 that the child was eligible for the Norwood procedure, the first of three open-heart surgeries generally used to treat HLHS.

Gilkar and Ahmed consented to the surgery, which was performed Aug. 17, he said. At the time, Budner described the baby’s condition as "critical and complex."

BOARD-CERTIFIED OBGYN WARNS NEW MASSACHUSETTS LATE-TERM ABORTION LAW EXPOSES MOTHERS TO DANGER

McKenna West arrives for a Dallas court hearing in the surrogate custody dispute. (LM Otero/AP Photo)

West’s lawyers have argued that the court should make sure the baby continues to receive life-saving care. West told the judge she would abandon her custody request if the court determines the intended parents are committed to that care, according to the AP.

Gilkar and Ahmed have asked the court to delay a hearing over the temporary restraining order that gave them custody while the legal fight continues, TMZ reported.

TWO FAMILIES SUE NORTH DAKOTA HOSPITAL ON ALLEGATIONS BABIES WERE SWITCHED AT BIRTH

The custody battle is only one part of the couple’s broader legal fight with West.

Before the baby was born, Gilkar and Ahmed filed counterclaims seeking more than $100,000, alleging West breached their surrogacy agreement and caused them emotional distress. The counterclaims, obtained by TMZ, said the couple paid West $60,000 during the pregnancy under an agreement that addressed termination. West has denied wrongdoing and asked the court to dismiss the claims.

DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH

The dispute has only grown more personal since the baby’s Aug. 12 birth. West said in a New York Post opinion piece last week that she had only about a minute with the newborn, while his umbilical cord was still attached, before he was taken away. A court order has since barred her from seeing or holding the baby.

On Tuesday, the judge left that order in place and did not immediately decide the larger question of custody or conservatorship, according to the AP.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secured an emergency court order before the birth directing that medically necessary care not be delayed or obstructed, Fox News Digital previously reported. Paxton’s office also notified two Dallas medical centers of their obligations to provide life-saving treatment.

The Associated Press and Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Hochul remains defiant after sheriffs sue over law banning cooperation with ICE: 'Bring it on'
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump criticizes New York Gov. Kathy Hochul’s sanctuary policies while speaking at the Nassau County Police Academy Center for Training and Intelligence.

More than a dozen New York s...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump criticizes New York Gov. Kathy Hochul’s sanctuary policies while speaking at the Nassau County Police Academy Center for Training and Intelligence.

More than a dozen New York sheriffs are suing over a state law prohibiting law enforcement from entering into or maintaining certain agreements with ICE for civil immigration enforcement, as Gov. Kathy Hochul dared the agency heads to "bring it on."

A federal lawsuit led by Rensselaer County Sheriff Kyle Bourgault argues that the law is unconstitutional and unlawfully restricts elected sheriffs’ ability to enter into federally authorized immigration-enforcement agreements.

"Today, Kathy Hochul escalated her administration’s war on the police and she expanded polices to put criminals before the citizens of New York," Rensselaer County Executive Steve McLaughlin said on Tuesday.

The Local Cops, Local Crimes Act, which Hochul signed in May, took effect on Tuesday, barring local and state law enforcement agencies from entering into partnerships with federal authorities to assist on civil immigration matters. The law also bars new agreements to house civil immigration detainees; existing detention agreements must be terminated under their applicable termination provisions within three months of the law’s effective date.

BORDER CZAR HOMAN VOWS TO 'FLOOD' NEW YORK WITH ICE AGENTS DESPITE HOCHUL'S RESISTANCE

More than a dozen New York sheriffs are suing over a state law prohibiting law enforcement from cooperating with ICE. (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Police may still assist ICE in cases of violent or other forms of non-immigration crime, but officers may not divert local resources to help with civil immigration enforcement as part of an effort to advance President Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda.

Hochul threatened to sue localities that refuse to end cooperation agreements with ICE, setting up a confrontation between herself and her Republican challenger, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, as his county is among those with agreements with ICE.

"No county executive should think that they are above the law in the state of New York," Hochul said at a press conference on Tuesday.

She said any police department or sheriff’s office that ignores the law and maintains an agreement with ICE will face legal action.

"And to those suing us, those trying to block the implementation of this law who’ve tried before and failed, our law has already been upheld by the courts, but if you try me again, I say, bring it on," the governor declared.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS NEW YORK LAW BANNING ICE AGENTS FROM WEARING MASKS

The law, which the governor signed in May, took effect on Tuesday. (John Moore/Getty Images)

New York Attorney General Letitia James also issued subpoenas to law enforcement agencies that either did not confirm plans to end their agreements or failed to provide what her office viewed as a satisfactory response. The subpoenas were sent to the sheriff's offices of Broome, Steuben, Nassau and Rensselaer counties, as well as the Nassau County Police Department.

If the agencies fail to comply, the attorney general is vowing to file a civil suit, a spokesperson for her office told CBS News.

Hochul has said law enforcement will assist ICE "only if a real crime has been committed" but officers cannot use resources to help on civil immigration matters.

"Because we need local cops hunting down criminals, not kindergartners. Breaking up drug rings, not breaking up families. Arresting gun runners, not grandmas," Hochul said.

Blakeman, who held a press conference at the same time as Hochul's, did not address whether he would comply with the state's orders, but he later told the New York Post he would "probably" join the sheriffs' lawsuit.

New York Attorney General Letitia James also issued subpoenas to law enforcement agencies that did not confirm plans to end their agreements with ICE. (REUTERS/David Dee Delgado)

He has previously defended working with ICE to remove illegal immigrants, claiming at a recent event with Trump that about 2,000 of these individuals in his county have criminal records.

"Kathy Hochul, where do you want those guns? What neighborhood do you want to destroy? Where do you want those drugs? What community do you want to destroy? Where do you want those illegal immigrants with criminal records to live? You want it back in New York? We say no," Blakeman said at the time.

The Department of Homeland Security said Hochul "must stop putting politics above public safety."

"This type of insanity leads to more crimes and more innocent victims," a department spokesperson told the New York Post.

articles.title: Attempted drone incursion at Virginia prison leads to $324K contraband haul with meth, 17 cellphones
articles.excerpt: The Justice Department announced charges against 12 people for a sophisticated drone smuggling operation introducing dangerous contraband into federal prisons across multiple states. Former federal pr...
articles.body_text:
The Justice Department announced charges against 12 people for a sophisticated drone smuggling operation introducing dangerous contraband into federal prisons across multiple states. Former federal prosecutor Jim Trusty discuss the challenges of catching drones, which were used for 38 deliveries of drugs, cell phones and weapons to 10 facilities.

Virginia prison officials intercepted a package containing an estimated $324,000 worth of contraband, including a pound of suspected methamphetamine and more than a dozen cellphones, following an attempted drone incursion at a state prison, authorities said.

The Virginia Department of Corrections (VADOC) said corrections staff discovered the "suspicious package" at Sussex I State Prison at around 1:30 a.m. Monday.

Inside, officials said they found a one-pound bag of suspected methamphetamine, 17 cellphones with charging cables and 20 sheets of paper that appeared to be saturated with an unknown liquid.

FEDERAL INMATES MAY SOON GET TABLETS WITH MESSAGING CAPABILITIES AS BUREAU OF PRISONS MAKES MODERNIZATION PUSH

Virginia prison officials intercepted a package containing an estimated $324,000 in contraband following an attempted drone incursion at Sussex I State Prison. (Virginia Department of Corrections)

The agency said it also seized multiple hex wrenches, three USB Wi-Fi adapters and two SIM cards.

Officials also discovered an unusual assortment of other items, including 30 disposable lighters, two cartons of cigarettes, one pound of loose-leaf tobacco, three packs of cigars, two bottles of professional-grade tattoo ink, two bottles of perfume and two bottles of glue.

WILD VIDEO SHOWS INMATES RIOTING INSIDE JAIL AFTER FRUSTRATIONS OVER ACCESS BOIL OVER

Virginia corrections officials intercepted a package containing a pound of suspected methamphetamine, 17 cellphones and other contraband with an estimated "prison value" of approximately $324,000. (Virginia Department of Corrections)

VADOC estimated the contraband had a combined value of roughly $324,000 inside the prison.

VADOC Director Joseph Walters said the seizure highlighted the sophisticated methods people may use in attempts to smuggle contraband into correctional facilities.

DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS

Virginia prison officials said an attempted drone incursion at Sussex I State Prison led to the discovery of a package containing approximately $324,000 worth of contraband. (Photo by Long Wei/VCG via Getty Images)

"This investigation is an important reminder that some people will use sophisticated methods in an attempt to smuggle drugs and other dangerous contraband into Virginia Department of Corrections facilities," Walters said in a statement.

"I thank our institutional staff at Sussex I State Prison for their vigilance and focus on ensuring the safety and security of our facility," he continued. "Our dedicated correctional staff and OLES members stand ready to intercept any dangerous contraband that individuals may attempt to introduce into correctional settings to ensure the safety and security of our dedicated corrections team members, of incarcerated individuals in our custody, of probationers, and of people in communities all across the Commonwealth of Virginia."

The incident remains under investigation by VADOC's Office of Law Enforcement Services (OLES).

Anyone with information about attempted smuggling into a VADOC facility is asked to call OLES at 540-830-9280.

Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

articles.title: Falcons' starting QB post is Michael Penix Jr's to lose amid Tua Tagovailoa's struggles: report
articles.excerpt: Former NFL QB Brian Hoyer joins Danny Parkins and Coach Eric Mangini to discuss Deshaun Watson getting the Week 1 start for the Cleveland Browns, whether Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears can start...
articles.body_text:
Former NFL QB Brian Hoyer joins Danny Parkins and Coach Eric Mangini to discuss Deshaun Watson getting the Week 1 start for the Cleveland Browns, whether Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears can start the season hot, and who should get the starting nod for the Atlanta Falcons: Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr.

Tua Tagovailoa’s next chapter in the NFL isn’t going well at all, so much so that the Atlanta Falcons may have to rush Michael Penix Jr. back faster than they hoped.

When Tagovailoa joined the Falcons after being released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of this season, the team reportedly hoped he would play well enough in new head coach Kevin Stefanski’s offense that it would be comfortable starting the season with the veteran left-hander while Penix, coming off an ACL injury, had more time to recover.

However, ESPN/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport is reporting that the Falcons’ starting job is for Penix to lose at this point following Tagovailoa’s inconsistent play in training camp and the first preseason game.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Tua Tagovailoa of the Atlanta Falcons looks on during a joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts at Grand Park Sports Campus on Aug. 19, 2026, in Westfield, Ind. (Getty Images)

"It really seemed that the goal of the entire organization was to have Tua be the starting quarterback right away to start the season," Rapoport said. "Let Michael Penix come along slow. …Really you’d like him to be inactive for the first several games and really just take his time and make sure he’s fully healthy."

Tagovailoa has not set himself apart from the pack in terms of performance at camp, and he went 3-of-5 for 22 yards in the first preseason game against the Denver Broncos before Stefanski moved on to Jack Strand and Cooper Rush at quarterback for the rest of the contest.

"Tua’s play made that impossible, not just in the preseason game, which we’ve seen, but it sounds like practice as well. All of which is to say, this is Michael Penix’s job for the taking," Rapoport continued.

SEAN PAYTON TAKES VICIOUS SHOT AT FALCONS HOME CROWD AFTER HUMILIATING FIRST HALF

Tua Tagovailoa of the Atlanta Falcons warms up before the NFL preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Ga., on Aug. 14, 2026. (Getty Images)

In an ideal world, the Falcons hoped a fresh start for Tagovailoa would’ve been just what he needed for a heated training camp competition for the team’s starting job. Instead, with Penix getting back into the fold this week and splitting first-team reps, it appears they’re now hoping he can feel confident and, more importantly, be healthy enough to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1.

"Everything we do around this building is competing," Stefanski said. "I know it’s easy to say, ‘position battles,’ and those types of things, but we’re constantly competing. That’s not the focus for our guys. Our guys are pushing each other by showing up and putting in the work."

Then again, perhaps Tagovailoa’s play in the final preseason game against his former Dolphins squad can boost his confidence and chances at the starting job this Friday.

Dec 8, 2024; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up before the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. (Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images)

It’s not looking too good for him now, though, as Stefanski and his staff have an important decision to make before that Sept. 13 kickoff on the road in Pittsburgh.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Productivity Commission says ‘line was crossed’ when WA premier labelled them ‘east coast clowns’ over GST
articles.excerpt:
Commissioner Angela Jackson also said it was ‘disappointing’ that Anthony Albanese had ruled out changes to Western Australia’s GST arrangements

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates...
articles.body_text:
Commissioner Angela Jackson also said it was ‘disappointing’ that Anthony Albanese had ruled out changes to Western Australia’s GST arrangements

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Productivity Commission has condemned attacks on its integrity as “unacceptable” after its scathing assessment of Western Australia’s sweetheart GST deal as a costly mistake sparked a fierce political backlash and name-calling.

Angela Jackson, a productivity commissioner and co-author of the report, said the country’s leading independent economic advisory body welcomed criticism and comments on its work.

But Jackson said comments from Roger Cook, the Western Australian premier, lampooning the PC as “east coast clowns” and describing the report as deceitful had “crossed a line”.

“We are used to public debate. In fact, we welcome it at the Productivity Commission, it’s why we have interim reports,” she told ABC radio before a meeting of national cabinet on Wednesday afternoon.

“We are aiming, of course, to inform public policy debate, which can often get heated. Our view is that a line was crossed in terms of the nature of those comments from the Western Australian premier.”

Jackson linked the tone of the criticism and the language used “to attack our integrity” with “something that more broadly we are seeing in public debate internationally”.

“We want to call this out as being unacceptable.”

The commission was asked to review the 2018 legislation put in place under the Morrison government.

That deal fundamentally changed the way the commonwealth distributed the GST pool between the states and territories.

The commission’s interim report found that the 2018 legislation had achieved none of its objectives, made the system less fair and had funnelled an extra $23bn in taxpayer money to the nation’s richest state.

The interim recommendation to reverse the deal was backed by all other states and territories, but was immediately declared dead in the water by Anthony Albanese.

“What I believe is, very clearly, there will be no change to WA GST arrangements whilst I’m prime minister,” Albanese said on Monday.

Jackson said Albanese’s comments were “disappointing at this point in the process”.

The PC will now do further consultation before a final report due by the end of this year.

“It’s important for us to indicate that that process will not be influenced by the prime minister’s comments, that we are above politics,” Jackson said.

“And that’s a very important position that we hold within the public policy landscape in Australia.”

On Wednesday, the industry and science minister, Tim Ayres, said there were “strong views” about the GST issue in WA, and a “colourful contest” about the issue when asked about Cook’s comments.

“The Productivity Commission has important work to do for Australia and we’re not a government that gets reports that contest our view and has a glass jaw about that,” Ayres told the ABC.

Ayres claimed WA was a state with “particular needs” and defended Albanese ruling out any GST changes even before the PC’s final report.

“[Albanese] gets Western Australia, understands what Western Australians need and the contribution that they make. And everything he’s done has been completely consistent with that view and it should have surprised nobody.”

Cook’s office has been approached for comment.

articles.title: US halts all immigrant visa applications amid tightening restrictions
articles.excerpt:
Move by state department to limit access is part of Trump’s crackdown on both lawful and undocumented immigration

All US immigrant visa applications have been paused by the Trump administration as th...
articles.body_text:
Move by state department to limit access is part of Trump’s crackdown on both lawful and undocumented immigration

All US immigrant visa applications have been paused by the Trump administration as the state department moves to tighten restrictions and limit access to applicants who they deem could end up relying on US assistance, a state department official confirmed Tuesday.

The agency launched the initiative at all embassies and consulates in early August, according to the official and visa appointments had to be adjusted to accommodate “in-depth training”, according to the official. The state department has been working on updated guidance and training since early this year, “to ensure all consular officers are fully equipped to evaluate every visa applicant comprehensively and consistently”, they added.

Financial Times reports that applicants with interviews already scheduled were sent emails that their appointments had been canceled and that they would be informed of a new date and time.

Agency officials claim this will ensure visa applicants will not end up relying on US public benefits. But it’s part of a slate of strategies the Trump administration has employed to crack down on both lawful and undocumented immigration and create a more selective process for who can gain entry into the system.

This week the Trump administration also announced plans to revoke visas from asylum seekers who initially entered the country for tourism or business. Up to 200,000 people currently seeking asylum could be impacted, marking what would end up being the largest mass pulling of visas in the history of the US. The action is being taken in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security.

Under Trump, visa applicants have also faced new restrictions, including review of their social media histories and added costs for processing, the Associated Press reported.

The pause on new visas and training program follows an attempt by Trump to block applications on a similar “public charge” basis, which included a block on applications from 75 countries selected by the administration, which was recently overturned by a federal judge.

“The court made clear that immigration laws cannot be used to justify discrimination,” Joanna Cuevas Ingram, senior staff attorney at the National Immigration Law Center said in a statement last week. “We are determined to ensure every person and family this ban harmed receives appropriate relief and will continue to hold this administration accountable to its obligations under the law.”

In February, a federal judge overturned the president’s attempt to suspend the US refugee system entirely. Federal agents, under Trump, have been allowed to block asylum seekers from entering the US, a move that human rights advocates said undermines international asylum laws.

The latest attempt to restrict access will cause immediate obstacles for those who have lawfully abided by an already challenging process, according to immigration law experts.

Many applicants impacted by the pause likely “spent thousands of dollars and disrupted their lives to attend scheduled interviews, only to have their appointments cancelled at the last minute”, Brian Simmons, an attorney at immigration law firm Fragomen in Washington told FT. It’s unclear when those appointments will be rescheduled.

articles.title: Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball hires driver following reckless driving incidents in Charlotte, brother Lonzo says
articles.excerpt: The Charlotte Hornets beat the Miami Heat 127-126 in OT thanks to a LaMelo Ball game winner. Colin Cowherd asks if the play-in tournament is good for the league and discusses what the Hornets proved i...
articles.body_text:
The Charlotte Hornets beat the Miami Heat 127-126 in OT thanks to a LaMelo Ball game winner. Colin Cowherd asks if the play-in tournament is good for the league and discusses what the Hornets proved in this win.

LaMelo Ball’s extensive car collection has drawn attention since his rise to basketball stardom. But the Minnesota Timberwolves guard has now decided to employ a personal driver to help him get around his new NBA home, according to his older brother, Lonzo Ball.

During a recent edition of the "Curious Mike" podcast, Lonzo Ball pointed to his younger brother while discussing which member of the Ball family spends the most money with Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr.

"Who in your family out of y'all three spends the most [money]," Porter asked.

"The one who has the most, LaMelo," Lonzo replied.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

LaMelo Ball's Charlotte penthouse has gone viral for its unique decor as the point Guard moves to Minnesota after a trade to the Timberwolves earlier this offseason. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images)

"[He's] got 10 cars," Lonzo continued. Having a driver could mean the 25-year-old spends less time behind the wheel and, in turn, has fewer opportunities to be involved in an accident.

Lonzo also suggested LaMelo could benefit from choosing vehicles outside the exotic-car category, rather than Lamborghinis and similar high-performance models he has owned in the past.

LAMELO BALL'S CUSTOM HUMMER LOSES WHEEL IN CHARLOTTE CRASH DURING ALL-STAR BREAK

"He'll buy a $1 million car and then just immediately f–k it up, I've never understood [that]," Lonzo added in reference to his sibling's habits when it comes to vehicles. "You just bought that? And then you ripped it up? You could've just got a beater," the former Los Angeles Lakers guard noted.

Lonzo then addressed the perception surrounding the frequency of LaMelo’s road incidents, saying his younger brother "doesn’t get into accidents, but he has a lot of situations on the road."

Chicago Bulls guard Lonzo Ball (2) hugs brother Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball (2) after an NBA game on Nov. 29, 2021 in Chicago, Illinois. (AP Photo/Paul Beaty)

The Lakers selected Lonzo Ball with the second overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. He later played for the New Orleans Pelicans and Chicago Bulls before joining the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2025. The Cavaliers traded him to the Utah Jazz in February 2026, but the Jazz subsequently waived him before he appeared in a game for the team.

Lonzo's NBA career has been marked by injuries. After appearing in 35 games during the 2021-22 season, he spent more than two calendar years sidelined.

Chicago Bulls guard Lonzo Ball and Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball look on during the second quarter at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois, on Jan. 17, 2025. (Luke Hales/Getty Images))

"It was like a 1,000 and something days," Ball said, reflecting on the length of his absence. He added that he has come to terms with the possibility that he may not return to the same level he once reached as an athlete.

"I came at peace with that when I got hurt the first time. Every time you get hurt it kind of sets you back," Ball told Porter.

The Hornets selected LaMelo with the third overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. Charlotte traded the two-time All-Star guard and his teammates Josh Green to the Timberwolves in June for Naz Reid and multiple draft picks.

Chantz Martin is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Pritzker’s swagger stunt backfires as critics roast viral video: ‘Cringiest thing he’s ever posted’
articles.excerpt:
‘The Five’ co-hosts comment on Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker coming under fire for being 'out-of-touch' for his National Walking Day video.

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker showed off his swagger in a tongue-in...
articles.body_text:
‘The Five’ co-hosts comment on Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker coming under fire for being 'out-of-touch' for his National Walking Day video.

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker showed off his swagger in a tongue-in-cheek social media video Monday, prompting a wave of mockery from critics online.

The video, recorded in black and white and notching more than 1 million views, features Pritzker making a variety of model-like expressions at the camera behind a caption that reads "when you’re in an aura-farming contest and your opponent in JB." Aura-farming is a common piece of slang used to describe the taking of certain actions with the explicit goal of acquiring swag.

Many social media users did not agree with Pritzker’s assessment of himself.

PROGRESSIVE MINNEAPOLIS MAYOR'S VIRAL HIP-HOP MOVES SPARK 'HUMILIATION RITUAL' MOCKERY ONLINE

Post made to Gov. JB Pritzker's X account on Aug. 24. (X/@JBPritzker)

"Only thing bigger than the ratio this tweet is getting is…well," White House deputy assistant to the president Kaelan Dorr posted in response to the video.

"Pritzker is kind of a medical marvel," conservative commentator Matt Walsh wrote. "He looks gaunt and frail from Ozempic and also still morbidly obese at the exact same time. He's taking the concept of ‘skinny fat’ to places never thought possible."

WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK AFTER 'SLOB' JB PRITZKER SAYS TRUMP IS SUFFERING FROM 'DEMENTIA'

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker holds a news conference in Chicago, Wednesday, June 24, 2026, to sign the Reproductive Health Records Privacy Act (HB 5295) into law. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Pritzker wrote the phrase "governor-maxxing" alongside his video on X. "Maxxing" as a suffix denotes that someone is doing something in a highly optimized way. "Looks-maxxing," for instance, refers to the act of taking one's appearance, physical fitness, and demeanor seriously as to maximize attractiveness.

Some on social media used the governor’s phrasing to poke fun at him.

Brian Costin, who is a high-level staffer at a right-of-center advocacy group in Illinois, accused Pritzker of "property-tax-maxxing," "state-and-local-tax-burden-maxxing," "cell-phone-tax-maxxing," "gas-tax-hike-maxxing," and "blaming-everyone-else-maxxing," among other things.

Others focused on his weight, claiming that Pritzker was "buffet-maxxing" or "waistline-maxxing."

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker speaks to members of the media at Manny's Cafeteria and Delicatessen during a primary election in Chicago, Illinois, on Tuesday, March 17, 2026. A Senate Democratic primary in Illinois to pick the successor to Senator Dick Durbin could turn on campaign dollars and differences on immigration policy (Credit: Christopher Dilts / Bloomberg via Getty Images)

REPUBLICANS RIP 4 BLUE STATES FOR KEEPING TAXES ON TIPS, OVERTIME AFTER TRUMP REPRIEVE

"When you’re a grown nepo-kid and believe you’re as impressive as the people you’re paying say you are," Fox Business anchor David Asman said of Pritzker, whose father, Donald Pritzker, helped build the Hyatt hotel chain with his brother Jay.

Pritzker has a history of making widely mocked social media posts, including his frequent attempts to spar with the president.

"Might be the cringiest thing he's ever posted, and that is saying a lot," RealClearPolitics president Tom Bevan wrote.

Pritzker's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

articles.title: El-Sayed's defense of Sharia law stance sparks online eruption from Christians, conservatives: 'He's done'
articles.excerpt:
'Jesse Watters Primetime' host Jesse Watters calls out Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed's for his previous comments criticizing the banning of Sharia Law.

Michigan Democratic Senate ...
articles.body_text:
'Jesse Watters Primetime' host Jesse Watters calls out Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed's for his previous comments criticizing the banning of Sharia Law.

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed sparked controversy on social media Monday night after comparing Sharia law to Christian canon law during an interview with Fox News anchor Jesse Watters.

"Getting rid of Sharia law is White supremacy?" Watters said to El-Sayed, bringing up past comments from the Michigan candidate opposing a ban on Sharia law and comparing those efforts to white supremacy. "Can you explain that one?"

Sayed responded by comparing Sharia, Islamic law based on religious texts, to Catholic Church law and governance.

"Nobody is trying to push Sharia law on anyone else, just like I hope nobody is trying to push Canon law on anybody else, because we live in an America where you should have the freedom of your religion," El-Sayed said.

TRUMP INAUGURATION PASTOR SAYS DEARBORN CHRISTIANS 'AFRAID' TO SPEAK OUT IN MUSLIM-MAJORITY CITY

Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed joined "Jesse Watters Primetime" on Monday. (Fox News)

The comparison sparked pushback on social media from users highlighting the differences between the two viewpoints and traditions.

"He lies and says no one is trying to push Sharia (they are), and draws a false equivalency to Christian Canon law," Charlie Kirk Show Executive Producer Andrew Kolvet posted on X. "Canon law determines how Christian leaders, churches, and Christians should live, but Canon law is limited to affairs of the Church (spiritual penalties). Canon law grants great autonomy to the state."

Kolvet continued, "Sharia law is MUCH more comprehensive, governing all aspects of life, and historically, and according to many contemporary Islamic clerics, dictates the affairs of the state."

EL-SAYED'S AGENDA PUTS ‘PERMANENTLY’ CHANGED AMERICA ON THE LINE IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE, GOP FIREBRAND WARNS

"Sharia law is incompatible with Western Civilization," political commentator Carl Jackson posted on X. "I’m tired of El-Sayed playing the victim card in attempt to avoid legitimate scrutiny of Islam."

"Yeah, it’s over for him," Fox News contributor Kaylee McGhee White posted on X. "Rogers by 6."

"@AbdulElSayed doesn’t get to bloviate about sharia being a mere ‘practice’ of faith when it’s Islamic jurisprudence used to supplant western jurisprudence," conservative commentator and radio host Dana Loesch posted on X.

"'Jesse, the Catholic Church requires ministers to use plant oils in sacraments with the blessings of a bishop, so why shouldn't courts allow Muslim men to have four wives?'" conservative commentator Michael Knowles posted on X.

"Canon law applies to Catholics," conservative commentator Pamela Geller posted on X. "There is no compulsion is Canon law. Jewish law applies only to Jews. There is no compulsion in Jewish law. It is voluntary. The sharia is a comprehensive legal system governing every aspect of human life, and asserts authority over non-Muslims."

"This was a very strange prepared defense from Abdul," GOP communicator Matt Whitlock posted on X. "I expected him to say it was out of context, not reflective of current views, etc. Instead he accepted the premise and defended promoting Sharia Law - opening that lane up to more attacks."

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, talks poolside with streamer Hasan Piker at a party for content creators supporting his campaign, Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment.

Abdul El-Sayed previously said he felt religiously obligated to follow Sharia-compliant practices in a 2009 interview with The New York Times.

"Ultimately, the question is, when I die and I stand before God and go through everything I did in my life, I don’t want to say I did it the easy way instead of the Shariah-compliant way," El-Sayed told the Times.

"Not because of fear but because of obligation."

Sharia law traditionally prescribed death for people who leave Islam, placed strict restrictions on what women can do and allowed child marriage.

El-Sayed has spoken out against bans on Sharia law, arguing such efforts are rooted in White supremacy.

"The state of Oklahoma voted in a referendum to amend the constitution to ban Shariah law. What does that mean? I don’t know. And yet the voters banned it anyway," he said in 2022. "The same exact forces that drove Native peoples from their land two centuries ago, destroyed Black Wall Street a century ago, bombed a building decades ago and tried to ban Sharia law not a decade ago, those forces are alive and well today.

"The reason I wanted to go all the way back to the 1830s is because you can’t understand a Sharia ban without understanding the Trail of Tears. You can’t understand the efforts to uproot Muslim Americans without understanding the Tulsa massacre. You cannot understand the challenges we face today without understanding white supremacy."

Fox News Digital’s Robert Schmad contributed to this report

Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

articles.title: Angel Reese tainted a historic WNBA night with a shameless late-game stat-padding layup
articles.excerpt:
Dan Dakich reacts to Angel Reese acting like a victim after being referred to as a "protected species" due to officiating favorability

Angel Reese had a historic night Monday against the Los Angeles ...
articles.body_text:
Dan Dakich reacts to Angel Reese acting like a victim after being referred to as a "protected species" due to officiating favorability

Angel Reese had a historic night Monday against the Los Angeles Sparks. She grabbed 26 rebounds in Atlanta's 78-71 win, breaking the WNBA single-game record (24) that Chamique Holdsclaw had held since 2003.

Her 20th rebound of the night also put her past A'ja Wilson for the most rebounds in a WNBA season.

Hitting the glass for 26 boards is an impressive record, no question (even if three of them were her patented "Mebounds"). But Reese and her Dream teammates tainted the historic night during the final 20 seconds.

ESPN TURNS ANGEL REESE’S 49 ‘MEBOUNDS’ INTO PROOF THAT SHE’S A LEGENDARY WNBA REBOUNDER

Atlanta led 76-69 with 20 seconds left and Reese had nine points. Following a Sparks possession that resulted in two missed shots, Dream guard Jordin Canada collected the rebound. It turns out that Reese never even attempted to play defense on the possession. Instead, she waited in the frontcourt for Atlanta to regain possession.

Angel Reese's 26 rebounds broke the WNBA single-game record, but a controversial uncontested layup in the final seconds raised stat-padding questions. (Getty Images)

Canada did just that and then heaved the ball the length of the court to a wide-open Angel Reese with 15 seconds left.

Reese had the ball with a seven-point lead, and no defender near her. All she had to do was dribble out the clock and secure the victory. But if you've been paying attention to Reese's career, you can probably guess what happened next. Reese scored on an uncontested layup, giving her 11 points on the night and her 27th double-double of the season.

Atlanta didn't need the points. Reese needed them.

If an NBA player did that, there's a chance a physical altercation might follow. Instead, everyone simply accepted that Reese is going to do whatever she has to do to make sure the box score looks the way she wants it to look.

To be clear, Reese didn't find herself one unlucky bounce short of 10 points. She went 4-for-14 from the field and was 3-for-13 before the layup. The WNBA.com play-by-play lists seven missed layup attempts and all 10 of her missed shots came within 5 feet of the basket.

She also had five shots blocked and Sparks forward Cameron Brink blocked four of them.

Brink is the Sparks' only legitimate healthy rim-protector, and Los Angeles came into the game 13-24. Reese kept attacking her, kept getting turned away and then got the one layup nobody contested after the result had already been decided.

Her 26 rebounds were already in the books. The late basket didn't help her reach either rebounding record. It took her from nine points to 11, and it got her to double-double No. 27. Not only that, but Reese didn't get back on defense during a possession that could have mattered to ensure that she got her points.

ANGEL REESE 'DIDN'T SLEEP' AFTER BLOWING GAME-WINNING LAYUP AGAINST FEVER, SMIRKING CAITLIN CLARK

Reese is now one double-double behind Alyssa Thomas' WNBA single-season record of 28 and she has six games left to tie it. Given that she and her teammates seem intent on making sure she gets her numbers, Reese should be a lock to break that record. But should it come with an asterisk?

This isn't the first time a Reese double-double has needed help after the actual basketball part of the game was finished.

In 2024, her former team, Chicago, was closing out a win over her current team, Atlanta, when Reese needed one point to keep her double-double streak alive. She had seven points and 11 rebounds entering the fourth quarter, but struggled to score in the final frame, missing two layups over the first nine minutes. With 25 seconds left, she finally converted a layup to give the Sky a five-point lead.

It was a crucial bucket for the team, but left Reese one point away from the 10 she needed.

Angel Reese has been accused of stat-padding back to her days with the Chicago Sky. (Scott Taetsch/Getty Images)

The Dream failed to score on their ensuing possession and the Sky hit two free throws after an intentional foul. Atlanta once again failed to score and was content to let the clock run out and end the game.

ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN

Rather than just dribble out the rest of the clock, like almost every basketball team does in that situation, Chicago guard Chennedy Carter decided to get the ball to Reese, who had her arms in the air and was calling for Carter to pass her the ball.

Clearly, Reese knew she needed those points to get into double-figures and, despite the game being over, she wasn't going to pass up the opportunity to pad the stats and add to her record.

Reese was then fouled by an Atlanta defender, and she made both free throws to extend her double-double streak to 14 straight games.

Monday's layup came with a different team and a different record on the line. But the results were eerily similar. Reese knew the exact number of points she needed, put herself in a position to get those points despite the game being essentially over, and made sure her teammates did their part to help her.

A reporter opened a postgame question by congratulating Reese on the "NBA record," then immediately corrected himself.

"Well, you know what I'm talking about," he said.

"No, I don't cuz I be setting NBA records, too," Reese replied.

Angel Reese grabbed 26 rebounds to break the WNBA single-game record against the Los Angeles Sparks, but an uncontested layup in the final seconds sparked stat padding criticism. (Tyler Ross/NBAE via Getty Images)

Look, the reporter obviously meant WNBA. Reese set WNBA rebounding records Monday night. She didn't set an NBA record because she plays in the WNBA, not the NBA.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Instead of laughing off the mistake and talking about her team's performance, she took the opening to brag about something that simply wasn't even true. Maybe she was joking, but it didn't sound like a joke.

It was an arrogant response to a reporter's verbal mistake, and it looks even worse after considering the stat-padding layup that she ended the game with.

Reese set two legitimate WNBA records on Monday. Then she cherry-picked two free points in a game Atlanta had already won because she just can't help herself.

articles.title: Mass arrests in global crackdown on West African cyber-crime networks
articles.excerpt:
Interpol says Operation Jackal IV demonstrates the power of international co-operation

Fifty-eight people linked to organised West African cyber-crime groups have been arrested in an operation across...
articles.body_text:
Interpol says Operation Jackal IV demonstrates the power of international co-operation

Fifty-eight people linked to organised West African cyber-crime groups have been arrested in an operation across 22 countries and six continents.

Dubbed  "Operation Jackal IV", it was co-ordinated by the global policing agency Interpol, targeting those behind romance and investment scams. It also identified 263 suspects.

Interpol said it was a response to the escalating global threat posed by these criminal networks - such as the feared Nigerian Black Axe group - believed to be behind a "significant share" of cyber-enabled financial fraud.

The operation also allowed analysis of emerging trends such as how these groups use sextortion to target minors, with victims as young as 14.

The ultra-violent cult that became a global mafia

Operation Jackal IV - which took place between November 2025 and June 2026 -  investigated how the groups laundered money and how financial fraud cyber crimes, such as cryptocurrency and email compromise fraud, were conducted.

Scams often targeted "retirees in English-speaking countries", Interpol said.

"By following illicit financial flows across borders, we are attacking the very lifeblood of organised crime and making it increasingly difficult for criminal networks to profit from their activities," Tomonobu Kaya, director of Interpol's financial crime centre, said in a statement.

"Operation Jackal IV demonstrates the power of international co-operation."

During the operation, Interpol helped with cross-border co-ordination and intelligence sharing.

It also provided support and specialised training for money-laundering investigations with the participating countries.

Interpol said many aspects of Jackal IV remained under investigation but preliminary outcomes included arrests in Argentina, Italy, Romania and South Africa.

In South Africa, seven sites linked to a syndicate involved in romance and investment scams were raided.

The policing agency was on scene in Johannesburg to support local authorities during the raids.

South African police made 39 arrests, seized $2.67m (£1.96m) and blocked 257 bank accounts.

As well as cyber-enabled fraud, the West African networks also participated in other serious and violent crimes, Interpol said.

Operation Jackal IV is one of multiple "Jackal" police operations that have taken place since 2022.

In 2024, Jackal III led to the arrests of 300 people linked to Black Axe and other affiliated groups.

Black Axe is a shadowy criminal network with trafficking, prostitution and killing operations around the world.

Nigeria is its main recruitment ground and many of its members are university educated and inducted during their schooling.
