articles.title: Vance says Canada friendlier to China on trade than to US: 'Insanity'
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Alex Hogan reports on the collapse of U.S.-Canada trade talks, which prompted 50% tariffs on $20 billion in Canadian goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney criticizes the ta...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Alex Hogan reports on the collapse of U.S.-Canada trade talks, which prompted 50% tariffs on $20 billion in Canadian goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney criticizes the tariffs, warning they will burden consumers.

President Donald Trump's trade talks with Canada have stalled – with threats of retaliatory tariffs ramping up again – but Vice President JD Vance was in Maine, explaining to voters that Canada has been friendlier to China on trade than to them, particularly farmers.

"They treat Chinese goods more fairly than they do the goods that come from the people of Maine: It’s insanity," Vance said during a question-and-answer session in Brewer, Maine, on Monday afternoon. "And what we’ve said to Canada is stop it."

Vance said he believes the U.S. and Canada had been close to reaching a trade agreement before negotiations broke down, blaming Ottawa for bringing what he described as "unreasonable last-minute demands" to the table.

TRUMP TRADE CHIEF WARNS CANADA WALKED AWAY FROM 'THE BEST DEAL' TO TRIGGER 50% U.S. TARIFFS

Vice President JD Vance thoroughly explained the basis of American protectionism to the voters in Brewer, Maine, calling out Canada for treating China more favorably on trade than it does for Mainers. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"I frankly thought we had a deal," Vance said. "I think that we should have a deal, but I think that we need to send a message loud and clear to the prime minister of Canada: Stop taking advantage of the people of Maine. Stop taking advantage of America. It’s over."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Friday that Canada was suspending negotiations. Trump posted Monday on Truth Social that he plans to impose 50% tariffs on Canadian-made vehicles, auto parts and steel beginning in January 2027.

"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," Trump wrote. "Their ridiculously high tariffs on our Farmers and farm products has made life impossible for these great American Patriots, and has long created a 60 Billion Dollar Deficit between our two Countries. Not sustainable, and NOT ANYMORE!"

TRUMP ALLIES PUSH TO ARM PRESIDENT WITH NEW TARIFF WEAPON TO PUNISH COUNTRIES 'RIPPING OFF' AMERICA

Vance made the remarks during an appearance at Compotech, a defense technology manufacturer in Brewer, as the vice president fielded a question about how the administration’s tariffs could affect Maine businesses and consumers.

"We’re very mindful of the fact that Maine is a border state with Canada," Vance said. "There’s a lot of cross-border transaction between Maine and Canada. And what we’re trying to do here is just make sure that Maine actually gets a fair deal."

Vance argued that Canada and China have been among the worst offenders when it comes to trade barriers against the U.S., while drawing a sharp distinction between what Washington expects from an economic competitor and from a longtime ally.

CHAD WOLF: AMERICA CANNOT IGNORE CHINA’S ECONOMIC ATTACK ON US INDUSTRY

"China, you of course expect — they’re our biggest economic competitor," Vance said. "I would expect that from China. I would not expect that from Canada."

Vance then briefly referred to Canada as a "state" before immediately correcting himself, referencing Trump's long-running trolling of Canada, teasing it as the 51st state.

"We have to remember Canada is a state — sorry, Freudian slip — that was actually an accident," Vance said. "Canada is a country that has underinvested in its military that quite literally would get invaded by a foreign country were it not for the umbrella of protection provided by the United States of America."

CHAD WOLF: CANADA CAN'T EXPECT FREE TRADE WHILE LEAVING OUR NORTHERN BORDER VULNERABLE

He argued that Canada had responded to that relationship by imposing trade restrictions on American products while expecting the U.S. not to retaliate.

"They apply ridiculous tariffs and other non-tariff duties on Maine products coming into Canada, and they don’t expect Maine or anybody else to fight back," Vance said. "We’re sick of that."

"We are actually going to fight back against unfair trade practices, whether it’s coming from China or Canada."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION EXPANDS 'PRODUCT OF USA' LABEL AS PUSH FOR AMERICAN-RAISED BEEF GROWS

Vance pointed specifically to dairy products, contrasting the treatment of Canadian products entering Maine with the tariffs that can apply when U.S. dairy exports exceed Canada’s tariff-rate quotas.

"If a Maine farmer sends dairy products into Canada, they could be paying as much as a 250% tariff," Vance said. "Now, how is it fair to the farmers of Maine that they pay 250% when the Canadian farmers pay nothing?"

CANADA REPORTEDLY SCRAPS JOINT BRIDGE CELEBRATION WITH US AFTER TRUMP RENEWS TARIFF THREAT

Canada’s dairy system provides duty-free access for set quantities of U.S. products under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, but steep tariffs can apply once imports exceed those quotas. Canada’s tariff schedule, for example, lists a 241% over-quota rate for certain milk products, while other dairy categories can carry even higher rates.

Vance also accused Canada of allowing Chinese goods to use the country as a route into the North American market, saying that issue had become part of the latest negotiations.

"We know that Canada allows itself to be used as a back door for Chinese goods," Vance said.

Vance nevertheless left open the possibility of the two sides returning to an agreement, even as he made clear the administration was prepared to keep tariffs in place without concessions from Ottawa.

"I think that we should have a deal," Vance said. "We expect fairness in our trade policy."

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

articles.title: Royce White predicts Enes Kanter Freedom will be suspended from WNBA events after run in with Natasha Cloud
articles.excerpt:
Former NBA player Royce White joins Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich to sound off on the viral WNBA controversy following Enes Kanter Freedom’s ejection from the Indiana Fever vs. Chicago Sky game.

Former ...
articles.body_text:
Former NBA player Royce White joins Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich to sound off on the viral WNBA controversy following Enes Kanter Freedom’s ejection from the Indiana Fever vs. Chicago Sky game.

Former NBA player Royce White believes Enes Kanter Freedom’s removal from a WNBA game following his exchange with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud may be only the beginning of the league’s response.

White, who, like Freedom, has officially declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft to challenge the league's eligibility policies, joined 'Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich' on Monday and shared his reaction to the now-viral moment that unfolded in Chicago on Sunday during the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Sky.

During a break in the action in the third quarter, Cloud began talking towards Freedom, who was sitting court side. The former NBA forward responded by stepping toward the floor, leading Cloud to approach him, before security got involved and escorted Freedom out of the arena.

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud #9 of the Chicago Sky yell at one another during the second half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on August 23, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) (Michael Reaves/Getty Images)

When asked by Dakich whether he believes Freedom may have made a mistake by getting involved with Cloud, White took things in a bit of a different direction, and predicted the WNBA will intervene with authority.

"I just know how the business works and how the PR works, and they're going to say that he instigated a conflict with a player, and there is an immutable line between the spectators and the players," White began.

"They're going to make a statement that he's, you know, indefinitely suspended or banned from WNBA events, if not NBA and WNBA. Same as the guy who was caught throwing the dildo on the court. Now it's a very different deal what that guy did and Enes, but they'll treat it the same because of the nature of the politics and the controversy. In my opinion, that statement is coming in the next couple of days."

SKY COACH PRAISES NATASHA CLOUD AFTER HEATED VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom looks on courtside during the first half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago on Aug. 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

After being escorted out of the arena, Freedom shared his side of what took place on the floor with Cloud.

"Sophie Cunningham shot a three, and I put my hands up to celebrate," Freedom told Jackson Thompson of Fox News Digital. "Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’

"And I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her.’ And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me, and literally I just got up, and then I was like, ‘I’m just here to protect women, and that’s all.’"

ENES KANTER FREEDOM OPENS UP ON CONFRONTATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD THAT LED TO EJECTION, WNBA PURSUIT

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom poses courtside prior to the game between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on Aug. 23, 2026, in Chicago, Ill. (Getty Images)

WNBA PLAYER NATASHA CLOUD FIRES OFF PRO-TRANS MESSAGE FOLLOWING ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM

Freedom also explained that Cloud began using "some very heavy language" towards him, which surprised him given the many young fans seated within shouting distance.

Freedom and White both declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft earlier this month after Fever star Sophie Cunningham received backlash for stating her opinion that women's sports should be exclusive to women. Freedom and White are using the league’s rules to challenge the WNBA to clarify its eligibility standards.

The WNBA’s current collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." It does not publicly define the term or establish specific eligibility requirements for transgender athletes.

articles.title: Reform would evict social housing tenants over unkempt gardens
articles.excerpt:
Plan part of a wider policy to remove foreign nationals from social homes and prioritise young British-born couples

Social housing tenants will be evicted if they fail to keep their gardens well main...
articles.body_text:
Plan part of a wider policy to remove foreign nationals from social homes and prioritise young British-born couples

Social housing tenants will be evicted if they fail to keep their gardens well maintained under a Reform UK government, the party has announced.

Lee Anderson, the party’s chair, said that if Reform came to power it would insist that those in social rented homes would be required to keep their properties decorated and gardens looked after.

The plan is part of a wider policy that would throw out any foreign national from their existing social home, and prioritise young married couples who were born in Britain for new housing.

Anderson told a press conference on Monday: “If you go back in time and look what actually happened … the people that rented council homes had to be married under a Labour, socialist government.

“They had to look after their property. They had to keep it well maintained. The gardens done and decorated, and they were inspected on a regular basis by officers from the council.”

He added: “What is wrong with expecting people who live in subsidised housing, paid for, subsidised, by the hard-working British taxpayer … to keep their house to a reasonable standard?”

The policy is part of a promise by Reform to oversee a boom in social housebuilding, whether through council or housing associations.

Richard Tice, the party’s deputy leader, said on Monday that Reform would change the law to make sure certain types of people got access to this new housing, with British-born working couples with children getting the highest priority.

Tice and Anderson said that for the purposes of the policy, people who were born abroad to British parents who were temporarily overseas would count as British-born. Those born abroad to foreign parents who have lived in the UK as British citizens for almost their entire lives, however, would not.

“We have no problem importing British-born people first,” Anderson said.

Tice, who is divorced and is getting remarried later this year, said his policy was deliberately designed to promote marriage.

“Marriage is a great thing, and in a sense, when people get married, we all hope that it’s going to be for life,” he said. “Sometimes it is, and sometimes it doesn’t work out, but I don’t think it’s wrong to be ambitious and to promote marriage.”

The party’s plans to boost social housebuilding rest largely on allowing housing associations, which have built the bulk of social homes since the Thatcher government, to borrow more.

Tice argued that if associations were allowed to increase the accounting value of the homes they own, they could borrow more and use that money to build.

Industry insiders, however, warned that such a plan could push many cash-strapped associations into worse financial problems.

Andy Hulme, the chief executive of Hyde, one of the country’s biggest housing associations, said: “As long-term charitable organisations that are closely regulated, social housing providers need to balance borrowing against the affordability of repayments.

“These proposals would radically change housing associations’ debt levels, which could lead many to violate their banking agreements and likely tip some into default.”

articles.title: Pennsylvania community raises thousands for small farm after carjacking left thousands in produce losses
articles.excerpt: A Pennsylvania farmer is reeling from a violent carjacking that destroyed his produce van and cost him thousands. The suspect attacked the driver, ransacked the vehicle, and ruined a valuable crop har...
articles.body_text:
A Pennsylvania farmer is reeling from a violent carjacking that destroyed his produce van and cost him thousands. The suspect attacked the driver, ransacked the vehicle, and ruined a valuable crop harvest.

A small Pennsylvania farm is facing thousands of dollars in losses after a barefoot carjacker allegedly attacked an employee and took off with a van packed with freshly harvested produce.

"It is really more surreal than traumatic," Hayday Farms owner Hank Whittenberg told Fox News on Monday.

"It was just a crazy situation at a stoplight where the man jumped onto the back of the van."

HEAR IT: MOM'S FRANTIC 911 CALL AFTER THIEF STEALS INSTACART DRIVER'S CAR WITH TODDLER INSIDE

This image aired on the Aug. 24 broadcast of "Fox & Friends First" shows ruined produce from Hayday Farms in Pennsylvania. (@Haydayfarmsorganics/Instagram)

The incident took place earlier this month when an employee on his way to a Philadelphia farmer's market was stopped at a traffic light and confronted by a man wearing scrubs.

Whittenberg said the employee was struck in the face during the confrontation, but is doing well despite suffering a black eye.

Bensalem police recovered the van two days later, but the five-acre farm was left facing thousands of dollars in losses after equipment was taken, the vehicle was damaged and much of the produce inside was left to rot.

"The van’s ripped up, equipment was taken," Whittenberg said, describing the lingering smell of rotting cantaloupes, tomatoes and corn inside the vehicle, which has since been replaced by the smell of chlorine and another scent he described as "mysterious."

HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS IN STOLEN GOODS RECOVERED AT A USED CAR LOT AFTER ADULT TOY COMPANY PURCHASE

Hank Whittenberg of Hayday Farms in Pennsylvania stands in the foreground with a van used by the farm in the background. (@Haydayfarmsorganics/Instagram)

Whittenberg told an area ABC affiliate that the perpetrator stole the cash box, a supply of honey and scales.

He said it could be several weeks before the van is back in service.

The costly setback prompted Whittenberg to launch a GoFundMe after supporters encouraged him to start one, with the community quickly rallying around the farm. As of Monday, the fundraiser had raised more than $11,000.

"We’re stunned with the response and just overwhelmed," Whittenberg said. "It really lets me know how much Philadelphia really stands behind us. It's really remarkable."

Taylor Penley is an associate editor for Fox News Digital and contributor to FOX Business and Fox Nation who covers media, culture and Flash

Conservativ...
articles.body_text:
Former Missouri congressional candidate Hartzell Gray explains why he believes his socialist platform represents the future of the Democratic Party as DSA-backed candidates pick up seats.

Conservatives are blasting the Charleston, South Carolina, chapter of Democratic Socialists of America after the group shared a Facebook ad seeking volunteers to provide child care at meetings and help support its "next generation of comrades."

"No experience with kids needed! Come ready to learn how to grow and support our next generation of comrades," DSA Charleston posted to its Facebook page Friday. "If you'd like to help support our next generation of comrades, join this training to review best practices, roleplay through scenarios, and get you feeling confident to welcome and care for our budding comrades."

The group is offering the virtual Zoom training Monday evening to adults with or without children.

The training comes as DSA’s influence within Democratic politics is growing, with socialist candidates notching primary wins as the midterm campaign intensifies and giving the organization a broader platform for its policies and organizing.

DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE

New York City Democratic mayoral nominee Zohran Mamdani delivers remarks in the Bronx, New York City, on Friday, Oct. 24, 2025. (Fox News Digital/Deirdre Heavey)

Critics accused the group of using "indoctrination" tactics, arguing the training reflects a broader push by socialists to court children.

"DSA childhood training for future 'comrades' in SOUTH CAROLINA! These people must be investigated," South Carolina Freedom Caucus founding chairman Adam Morgan wrote.

"They’re indoctrinating them as much as possible and it’s disgusting," said another user.

"They used to tell us socialism was just a Republican talking point. Now they’re advertising meetings for their ‘comrades.’ Socialism isn’t coming to South Carolina — it’s already here. And we CANNOT afford to ignore it. Far-left socialist groups are organizing in our communities and targeting the next generation with their radical agenda," wrote the South Carolina Republican Party account.

South Carolina is solid Republican territory, with President Donald Trump carrying the state by nearly 18 points in 2024 after Republicans won it in every presidential election dating back to 1980.

INSIDE TEACHERS' UNION MAY DAY 'DRESS REHEARSAL' CRITICS WARN WILL 'GROOM' STUDENTS INTO DEM 'FOOT SOLDIERS'

On Inauguration Day on Jan. 20, 2025, Democratic Socialists of America members marched in Washington, D.C., carrying signs that said, "SOCIALISM BEATS FASCISM," equating the incoming Trump administration to "fascism." A new report says that language parrots the rhetoric of foreign adversaries. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)

"Indoctrinate them young before they can become free thinkers," said one user.

In March, the chapter held their first "Comrades With Kids hangout" in which parents were invited to bring their kids to participate in card games, crafts, and other activities, Fox News Digital found, according to a prior social media post.

"Do you see what’s happening?? Mamdani is offering ‘free’ babysitting so they could turn your kids into socialists. They’re doing this all over the country," wrote popular conservative accounts Libs of TikTok.

Separately, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist, has made child care a central part of his agenda, including through the city's new "Parents’ Night Out" program.

Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside a Trump-owned building on May Day, May 1, 2019, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Mamdani's new pilot program titled, "Parents' Night Out," offers free-of-charge babysitting to parents for one night.

Nearly 300 children attended the Aug. 16 program at NYC Parks recreation centers across all five boroughs from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Through a separate partnership with the Department of Cultural Affairs, parents were offered free and low-cost cultural experiences while their children participated in the program.

Fox News Digital reached out Mamdani’s office and DSA Charleston.

Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: WNBA fight over males in women's sports exposes how the left keeps answering a question nobody asked
articles.excerpt: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham demands a 'bold' commissioner for the league as fans rally to support her stance on protecting women's sports. 'The Faulkner Focus' details the growing controversy, includi...
articles.body_text:
WNBA star Sophie Cunningham demands a 'bold' commissioner for the league as fans rally to support her stance on protecting women's sports. 'The Faulkner Focus' details the growing controversy, including a Seattle columnist who resigned over censorship.

WNBA player Natasha Cloud had a message for transgender people Sunday night.

The Chicago Sky guard wrote on social media that trans people "belong," that they're loved, seen and "perfect as you are." She added that they would always be "protected" by her.

WNBA HAS 'NO IDEA WHAT THEY'RE ABOUT TO FACE,' ENES KANTER FREEDOM SAYS AS LEAGUE TAKES ON TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE

It came after Cloud confronted Enes Kanter Freedom during the Sky's 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on Sunday night. Freedom has spent the past few weeks pushing the WNBA on something that really shouldn't be difficult to answer: Can a male play in a women's professional basketball league?

Natasha Cloud said trans people "belong" after confronting Enes Kanter Freedom, but the WNBA still hasn't answered the real eligibility question. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh)

The fight isn't over who gets through the doors at a WNBA arena. Freedom is asking whether a male is allowed to play in a women's league. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has made the same basic point, saying "biological men" shouldn't compete in women's sports.

But there's a reason the conversation keeps getting dragged somewhere else: defending males in women's sports is a much harder argument to make than simply declaring "trans people belong."

And Cloud wasn't the only one doing this over the weekend.

The New York Liberty hosted the Fever at Barclays Center on Saturday, and the scoreboard featured messages specifically welcoming transgender fans.

"Welcome Trans Liberty fans! You are loved and you belong!" one read.

Another said, "Hey trans fans! Glad you're here! Go Liberty!"

WOMAN CLAIMS NY LIBERTY TRIED TO CHANGE HER 'XX-XY' PAID SCOREBOARD MESSAGE FOR HALFTIME OF FEVER GAME

Outside the arena, transgender activists showed up to counter a rally supporting Cunningham and chanted "trans lives matter."

New York Liberty scoreboard at Barclays Center displays pro-trans messaging. (Fox News)

Transgender fans are welcome at basketball games. Treat them like everyone else in the building.

Because the response to Cunningham is a perfect example of what’s been happening in this debate for years.

Back in 2023, USA Today columnist Nancy Armour went after ESPN's Sam Ponder for supporting fairness in women's sports.

Armour called Ponder's position "bigotry" and accused Riley Gaines and others fighting to keep males out of women's sports of promoting hate.

I wrote at the time that Gaines wasn't "anti-trans." She was pro-woman.

Gaines' position has always been that the women's category should be reserved for females. You can disagree with her, but at least disagree with what she's actually saying.

Calling her a bigot or a transphobe is much easier than explaining why she's wrong.

A few months later, I went to Harvard when Riley Gaines spoke on campus. Before she even arrived, a Harvard athletic administrator had described her as an "athlete-turned-anti-trans-activist."

Rather than explain why Gaines was wrong about women's sports, the administrator branded her "anti-trans."

Riley Gaines and Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham pose for a photo following a WNBA game at Target Center. (Riley Gaines/XX-XY Athletics)

Then Martina Navratilova got the same treatment.

Navratilova has been one of the most outspoken female athletes in the country on this issue. She thinks women's sports should be for females.

A tennis reporter called her "transphobic" and accused her of going on an "anti-trans crusade."

Seriously. Explain why a male should be entitled to compete in a female athletic category. That's the hard part, so critics change the subject to hate, safety or claims that children struggling with gender identity need to be "protected."

And now the WNBA is doing its own version of the same thing.

For years, the playbook was simple: call anyone who objected a bigot or a transphobe.

Now the tactic is a little different. Don't defend males in women's sports. Just announce how much you love transgender people.

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt after Cunningham's comments started getting attention. Then came the Liberty scoreboard. Then Cloud's post.

But Cunningham wasn't talking about whether some kid somewhere feels like he or she "belongs."

"Trans Kids Belong" is a slogan, not an argument. And slogans become pretty useful when the logic isn't on your side. It still doesn't answer whether a male is eligible to play in the WNBA.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve wears a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt during a game against the Indiana Fever. (Star Tribune via Getty Images)

Freedom has forced the WNBA to confront that question.

He has publicly said he intends to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. Former NBA player Royce White has said the same. Obviously, they're making a point, and it's a useful one because the WNBA's own publicly cited eligibility language says only players who are women can play, but the league has not publicly defined the term.

So define "woman," WNBA. That shouldn't take multiple meetings over "weeks and months." The WNBA exists for female basketball players, which should mean a male isn't eligible.

And every time the question comes up, the WNBA drags the discussion back to hate, inclusion and protecting transgender people. Pretty soon we're miles away from the reason anyone started talking about this in the first place.

A trans fan can go to a Liberty game, buy a jersey and spend the night yelling at the refs like everyone else. Nobody's debating whether that person gets to sit in the stands.

We're talking about who gets to be on the court.

Turkish-American former basketball player and human rights activist Enes Kanter Freedom is seen prior to a game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Women's sports exist because sex matters in athletic competition. That's why female athletes have their own leagues, divisions and championships in the first place.

Keeping males out of women's sports isn't a statement about how anyone should be treated outside of sports.

Cloud can post whatever message she wants, and the Liberty can welcome trans fans on the scoreboard. Fine.

But the WNBA still hasn't answered the question that started this whole debate.

Should a male be allowed to compete in women's sports?

Maybe someday the people calling everyone else hateful will explain why they think the answer should be yes.

articles.title: Rupert Lowe set to be paid as much for divisive posts on Elon Musk’s X as for being MP
articles.excerpt:
Restore Britain leader paid up to £1,476 an hour by platform, which critics say is financially incentivising inflammatory content

Rupert Lowe, the leader of Restore Britain, is on course to earn as m...
articles.body_text:
Restore Britain leader paid up to £1,476 an hour by platform, which critics say is financially incentivising inflammatory content

Rupert Lowe, the leader of Restore Britain, is on course to earn as much from the social media platform X as he does from his salary as an MP, after surging income from posts that include demands for mass deportations.

Lowe has earned £932 an hour for his posts on X, formerly Twitter, since the start of the year, according to his own declarations in the register of MPs’ financial interests, which detail how many hours he has spent on X for each payment he received from the platform.

The figure is more than twice the £377 an hour on average he earned last year. His hourly rate rose steeply again this summer, reaching £1,476 since the start of June.

X critics claim it is further evidence that X is favouring and incentivising divisive political content, pulling the UK’s political discourse to the right. Elon Musk, the site’s owner, has repeatedly amplified Lowe’s posts.

Under X’s revenue-sharing scheme, premium subscribers such as Lowe are paid based on the performance of their posts. The scheme resulted in record payouts last year. The platform recently announced forthcoming changes, designed to reward original content and commentary.

Lowe’s total income from X since the 2024 general election has now surpassed £105,000. He earned more than half of that in the first eight months of 2026.

Should his average earnings for 2026 so far continue throughout the year, he would earn just over £93,000 – close to the current MPs’ £98,599 annual salary. He could easily exceed that figure should the higher rate of earnings of recent months persist.

Lowe has previously said he donates his net MP’s salary to charities and worthy causes in his constituency of Great Yarmouth.

The politician’s extraordinary success on X has led to concerns among some campaigners, who fear it is a sign that Musk’s site is effectively funding an MP that reflects the hard-right views of the billionaire.

“We tend to treat a politician’s online reach and their income as two separate stories, but for Rupert Lowe they’re part of the same mechanism,” said Ambrose Pym, a researcher covering the far right and technology who analysed Lowe’s rising X earnings. “The more his content is seen, the more X pays him for it.

“Scrutiny is rightly falling on other sources of foreign money in British politics. However, a US-based billionaire simultaneously paying and boosting an ideologically aligned British politician through his own platform is going strikingly under-reported. X’s financial and reach incentive structure rewards division and is shaping British politics with almost none of the scrutiny it deserves.”

Lowe, who founded Restore Britain after leaving Nigel Farage’s Reform UK, describes his party’s most significant achievement as “dragging mass deportations [of migrants] into mainstream politics”.

Asked about his accelerating X earnings, Lowe told the Guardian: “If I wanted to make money, I would not be in politics. I donate my entire net MP salary to local charities in my constituency – being a politician is the most expensive job I’ve ever had.”

His recent posts on X show the extraordinary amount of engagement the Restore leader secures on the platform. Over the weekend, one of his posts stated: “An illegal migrant could read ten thousand Home Office pamphlets in some woeful attempt to ‘integrate’, I’d still want him deported.

“They broke into our country – they are not welcome here, and they all need to be removed. This is not complicated.” It received 1.3m views, 25,000 likes and 3,000 reposts.

Last week, a post about how the UK should replicate Portugal’s ban on the burqa in many public spaces received almost a million views.

Lowe’s previous posts have included describing diversity policies as a “wicked, malicious, viperous cancer” and have criticised illegal migrants as “unvetted foreign males” loitering “where your daughter walks home”.

The Guardian has contacted X with a request for comment.

San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO John "Jed" York was arrest...
articles.body_text:
Steve Smith Sr. says Brandon Aiyuk is self-sabotaging his NFL career during a recent appearance on OutKick's "Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich."

San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO John "Jed" York was arrested and arraigned in East Palestine, Ohio on suspicion of "engaging in prostitution" and "possessing criminal tools" charges that were later amended to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, according to court records.

York was booked Sunday morning and released that afternoon on a $5,000 bond, the Columbiana County Sheriff’s Office confirmed to OutKick.

San Francisco 49ers CEO Jed York was arrested in August 2026 in East Palestine, Ohio. (Columbiana County Sheriff’s Office)

Owner Jed York of the San Francisco 49ers is seen on the field prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on December 15, 2022 in Seattle, Washington. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

The arrest occurred at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community – a trailer park.

East Palestine police referred OutKick to contact the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force for more information. The Task Force has not responded to a request for comment.

York appeared in Columbiana County Municipal Court on Monday morning. He pleaded no contest to the two misdemeanor charges after the prosecutor filed a plea agreement.

He must serve two days in jail, with one of those already credited for time served.

BRANDON AIYUK DROVE 104 MPH NEAR LEVI'S STADIUM AND FILMED IT, NOW A WARRANT HAS BEEN ISSUED FOR HIS ARREST

York was also ordered to pay $1,150 in fines.

York, 46, will be subject to NFL discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy.

"We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL told OutKick in a statement.

San Francisco 49ers chief executive officer Jed York is seen during pregame warmups prior to an NFL football game against the New York Giants at Levi's Stadium on September 21, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. (Ryan Kang/Getty Images)

The San Francisco 49ers have not commented.

York has been the majority owner of the 49ers since 2024 and was previously the team's CEO. He is originally from Youngstown, Ohio.

articles.title: Jeffries' reported meeting with Kushner about possible Trump cooperation draws left-wing backlash
articles.excerpt: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries faces intense backlash from far-left progressives on social media after holding a closed-door meeting with President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner. T...
articles.body_text:
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries faces intense backlash from far-left progressives on social media after holding a closed-door meeting with President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner. The two reportedly met to discuss how Democrats and the administration could work together, leading to accusations of betrayal.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner met in recent weeks and spoke about possible issues of common ground, according to reports, landing the top House Democrat in hot water with some on the political left who have taken issue with the reported get-together.

The men talked about housing, immigration and high living costs as possible categories of common ground, the New York Times reported. Kushner, the husband of Trump's daughter Ivanka, suggested that the lawmaker should meet with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, two individuals with knowledge of the meet-up noted, according to the outlet.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jeffries' offices and the White House on Monday.

KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO 'FINISH THE JOB'

Founder and CEO of Affinity Partners Jared Kushner attends the Allen & Company Sun Valley Conference at the Sun Valley Lodge on July 9, 2026 in Sun Valley, Idaho. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"Throughout this Congress, Republicans have adopted a my-way-or-the-highway approach to governing that has failed the American people. To stop the madness, we have repeatedly made clear that an extremist approach will not work and will be met with forceful opposition," Jeffries said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

"The American people want bold change and that’s what House Democrats will deliver. In every conversation that we have with the Trump administration, we will continue to make it explicitly clear that the affordability crisis is not a hoax and nothing short of transformational policy change is acceptable. We are fighting for an affordable America. The question is whether Republicans will join us," he said in the statement.

Some on the left have objected to the reported meeting between the congressman and Kushner.

SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: 'PACK OF FOOLS'

U.S. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., arrives onstage during "The New Power Structure: Black Politics in the Age of Resistance" panel during the 2026 National Association Of Black Journalists Convention at Atlanta Marriott Marquis on Aug. 13, 2026 in Atlanta, Ga. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)

Zeteo founder, CEO and editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan declared in a post on X, "The only meeting Hakeem Jeffries should be having with Jared Kushner is to tell him he’ll be subpoenaed by the House for a corruption investigation on day one of Democratic control of the House. This is just pathetic stuff from the House Dem leader."

Michelle Kinney, co-founder of The Mayday Network, wrote on X, "They should be f[—]ing hauling Jared Kushner in front of a committee, not MEETING with him. What in the absolute f— WE ARE ALL SO SICK OF THIS S— — ENOUGH!!!!"

Dean Obeidallah wrote on "The Dean's Report": "How could Jeffries not know the meeting would get leaked and it was the wrong thing to do?! This meeting doesn’t help Democrats win in November. In fact, now that we know about it, the result has been many Democrats slamming Jeffries online while some still defend him—causing a distraction to our real goal."

MIKE JOHNSON TAUNTS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR LOSING DEMS' CIVIL WAR 'IN HIS OWN BACKYARD'

The U.S. Capitol building is seen on Aug. 7, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

While Republicans currently hold a slight majority in the House of Representatives, Democrats have the opportunity to win the majority in the upcoming midterm elections.

If Democrats manage to flip control of the House, Jeffries would be a prime candidate for speaker.

Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott convicted of child sex abuse

articles.body_text:
Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott has been convicted of sexually abusing two children several decades ago in a trial in ⁠a Scottish court.

Dott was charged with two counts of “lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour” ⁠against a girl from 1993 to 1996 and a boy from 2006 to 2010.

The indictment alleged that the 49-year-old had sexually assaulted the girl, ‌exposed himself to her and induced her to touch him. Dott was also accused of making sexual remarks to the boy and touching his genitals.

He denied the charges but was found guilty on Monday after a trial ⁠at the High Court ⁠in Glasgow. He will be sentenced next month.

“Dott is a dangerous individual, and I hope this conviction provides some ⁠measure of comfort to those impacted by his crimes,” Detective Inspector ⁠Gary Smillie from Police ⁠Scotland told reporters.

Dott won the world snooker championship in 2006, beating Peter Ebdon 18-14 in the final, and ‌finished as runner-up in 2004 and 2010.

He was suspended by the World Professional Billiards and ‌Snooker ‌Association after the charges were announced last year.

articles.title: Burnham’s visit to Kyiv marks a renewal of badly needed support for Ukraine
articles.excerpt:
As well as pledging military help and diplomatic backing, the prime minister could be useful in dealing with the US

Since moving into Downing Street in July, Andy Burnham – a foreign policy neophyte ...
articles.body_text:
As well as pledging military help and diplomatic backing, the prime minister could be useful in dealing with the US

Since moving into Downing Street in July, Andy Burnham – a foreign policy neophyte – has expressed strong support for Ukraine. But on Monday he saw the bitter human cost of the war up close for the first time, visiting Kyiv during his first international trip as prime minister.

The occasion was the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence. Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave awards to the families of fallen soldiers. Relatives wept, hugging Ukraine’s president. Photos of young men in their prime were shown on a giant screen.

The setting was St Sophia cathedral in the old heart of the Ukrainian capital. Built in the 11th century, the building predates Moscow and is a symbol of Ukraine’s ancient statehood. Next to it were modern weapons used by Kyiv in its struggle against Russia including quadcopter drones and unmanned land robots.

In a speech in front of other western leaders, Burnham compared Ukraine’s fight to that waged by Britain during the darkest days of the second world war. “My nation kept the flame of European freedom alive in the 20th century, you hold that flame in the 21st,” he declared.

Like other high-profile visitors, Burnham arrived with a gift. Since 2023 the UK and France has been providing Kyiv with long-range Storm Shadow or Scalp (as the French version is known) cruise missiles, used to knock out Russian naval ships and command centres.

It was now handing over British blueprints for key components, Burnham said, so Ukraine could eventually make its own version with France.

More Storm Shadows could go some way to dealing with Ukraine’s biggest problem – the wave of ballistic missiles fired by Russia that rain down on Kyiv and other cities most nights. As of now, Ukraine has run out of US-made Patriotic interceptors capable of shooting them down. The Trump administration is disinclined to provide more.

The British cruise missiles carry a larger payload than the long-range drones favoured by Kyiv. They could be used to destroy enemy ballistic missile launch systems, which can be quickly moved, and are dotted around sites in western Russia. Depending on their range, they could also disable military runways and aerodromes.

But nobody expects production to start soon. In the meantime, the Kremlin has responded with characteristic belligerence. Vladimir Putin’s press spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said Moscow would destroy any Ukrainian Storm Shadow factories, and accused London of taking part in the war and adding “fuel to the fire” though it is France that is helping with building them.

Last week Russia threatened “consequences” over the supply of British drones to Kyiv and withdrew its ambassador from London. It is unclear how Putin might escalate further. He has already sent assassins to poison Russian dissidents on UK territory including the murder in 2006 of Alexander Litvinenko, killed with radioactive tea.

Burnham appears unmoved by what he dubbed “outrageous” Russian threats, an encouraging sign for Kyiv. On Monday he pointed out that it was Putin who “started the fire” with his illegal and unprovoked invasion, and assured Zelenskyy of his “personal commitment” to Kyiv’s existential cause.

Ukraine has warmly welcomed the Storm Shadow initiative. Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the Ukrainian parliament’s foreign affairs committee, told the Guardian he hoped manufacture could begin in “months, not years”. “We have proved many times we can do impossible things in producing weaponry,” he said, saying the missile “strengthened” Kyiv’s position in negotiations with Moscow.

Of Burnham’s visit, he added: “For us, it’s hugely symbolic and important. It illustrates that for the UK Ukraine remains a top priority. You are an important bridge and have rectified the situation whenever we have a crisis in our relations with the US. Your king is a valuable diplomatic tool and puts in a good word for us with Trump.”

The trip also signals to allies that the UK will continue to play a leading role in the coalition of the willing after the departure of Keir Starmer. Co-hosting a coalition meeting for the first time, Burnham said Europe would do everything it could to source more Patriotic interceptors for Ukraine. Zelenskyy has asked for 300 to help the country survive the coming winter.

Burnham’s speech made clear that he regards Ukraine’s struggle as Britain’s too – at a time when the US has effectively given up on its attempts to broker a peace deal, and has halted direct military aid. “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security but the frontline in keeping Europe safe,” he added. “The Ukrainian people deserve not just our continued support but our gratitude and respect,” he said.

Ukrainian leaders and soldiers are grateful for British diplomatic and moral support, though they know that London’s military power is limited. Storm Shadow is deemed to have been one of the UK’s most useful contributions but stockpiles were modest.

Ukraine’s focus has been on developing its own long-range drones and cruise missiles, such as Fire Point’s Flamingo, which have been used to strike refineries and warehouses deep inside Russia. The goal is to attack Russia with 1,000 drones and some missiles a day this year, not when Storm Shadow production lines are ready.

But the deal that Burnham has agreed with Zelenskyy is an important renewal of goodwill. At some point Zelenskyy will probably need the help of European allies whenever the White House re-engages with the peace process. Burnham may become an important interlocutor with Trump, and today’s trip is from Ukraine’s perspective an encouraging start.

Betrayal by Luke Harding (Guardian Faber, £20) is published on Thursday. To support the Guardian, order your copy at guardianbookshop.com. Delivery charges may apply.

articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza shelter extends casualty list
articles.excerpt:
An Israeli air strike has hit a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians in central Gaza, killing at least one person and wounding several others.

The attack happened early on Monday near al-Aqsa Hospi...
articles.body_text:
An Israeli air strike has hit a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians in central Gaza, killing at least one person and wounding several others.

The attack happened early on Monday near al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. The casualties add to the list of victims as Israel maintains its hostilities in the enclave.

In a post on Telegram, the Israeli army said it targeted two “militants” in the Deir al-Balah area on Sunday night including Muhammad Abdul Nasser Jaber Abu Asad, claiming he was a member of the elite forces of Hamas’s military wing and took part in the October 7 attack on Israel.

The army said the pair had recently been working to carry out operations against its forces and Israelis, and attempting to rebuild Hamas’s capabilities. The statement labelled the activities as a “systematic violation of the ceasefire”.

The ongoing strikes come despite a United States-brokered ceasefire to end Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, and amid diplomatic efforts to disarm Hamas and get Israeli troops to withdraw from the territory.

On Sunday three Palestinians, including a four-year-old child, were killed in Israeli strikes on areas including Khan Younis in southern Gaza and the town of az-Zawayda in the Deir al-Balah region.

A man who was wounded in an attack on Khan Younis in southern Gaza on Sunday died after succumbing to his wounds. Another, wounded in an Israeli airstrike on a cafe near Gaza Port last week, died on Monday.

A total of 1,288 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.

The total death toll since the war in Gaza was launched in October 2023 has risen to 73,422, with a further 174,401 wounded.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: LA ICE director reveals officers followed home, harassed as police fail to help in sanctuary city
articles.excerpt:
Los Angeles ICE Field Office Director Tom Giles breaks down the challenges of conducting immigration enforcement operations in one of America’s largest sanctuary cities.

EXCLUSIVE: From agents being ...
articles.body_text:
Los Angeles ICE Field Office Director Tom Giles breaks down the challenges of conducting immigration enforcement operations in one of America’s largest sanctuary cities.

EXCLUSIVE: From agents being followed home and harassed to dealing with riots and local police refusing to assist, ICE Los Angeles Field Office Director Thomas Giles gave Fox News Digital an inside look at the daily risks of conducting operations in one of America’s largest sanctuary cities.

Fox News Digital accompanied Giles and a team of ICE officers on an immigration enforcement operation in the Los Angeles area early Thursday morning. In an interview from inside his vehicle during the operation, Giles emphasized that while "it's not going to shut us down and stop us," California’s sanctuary policies put both his agents and the community at risk.

"The sanctuary policies definitely impact our operations in terms of it'd be a lot easier for us to have that transfer of custody in a secure environment," he explained. "So, what it does for us is it sends our officers out into the community, putting our officers at risk and other community members at risk to go out and try to apprehend this individual."

Fox News Digital witnessed ICE arrest six illegal immigrants Thursday morning, including one who had been convicted of assault with a baseball bat and another who had been convicted of illegally re-entering the U.S. multiple times.

DEADLY HOSPITAL STABBING PUTS NEWSOM UNDER PRESSURE OVER ICE DETAINER FIGHT

ICE Los Angeles Field Office Director Thomas Giles discusses operations in America’s second-largest city. (Fox News)

Giles explained that because of ongoing litigation in California, ICE officers are not allowed to knock on a target’s door or even set foot on the area surrounding the property. This complicates enforcement by forcing officers to apprehend targets in public spaces or through potentially dangerous vehicle stops.

He said that "before we had all these sanctuary policies … we were picking up hundreds of people a day at the local jails and bringing them in and processing them." Now, local law enforcement "can't even work with us," which he said "is definitely a big, huge public safety threat."

As an example, Giles pointed to one of the operation’s targets, 20-year-old Honduran national Julio Alberto Aroca-Rodriguez, whom local police had arrested the week before for assault with a deadly weapon using a baseball bat. Aroca-Rodriguez entered the U.S. at an unknown date and location and has been subject to a removal order since 2019. Local authorities declined to honor ICE’s request to hold Aroca-Rodriguez and released him.

When ICE officers encountered Aroca-Rodriguez on Thursday, they also detained four other "collaterals" identified as illegal immigrants. After making the arrests, the officers quickly relocated because a crowd of anti-ICE agitators had begun to form.

Giles described the treatment of ICE law enforcement officers by many California politicians, the media and members of the public as "degrading to the work that the men and women of ICE do."

EXCLUSIVE: 5-TIME ILLEGAL ENTRANT ADMITS ‘MISTAKE’ THAT FINALLY GOT HIM BUSTED BY ICE

"Death to ICE" is written on a garbage cart following multiple detentions by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), in downtown Los Angeles, California, U.S., June 6, 2025. REUTERS/Daniel Cole (REUTERS/Daniel Cole)

"My officers have been followed home and been harassed, harassed on social media, harassed just personally, and they get in your face and everything else," he said.

He also criticized anti-ICE agitators who wear masks while simultaneously "complaining about us wearing masks but they look the same as we do as well."

Despite this, Giles praised his officers as Americans who "love this country" and "want to support the Constitution."

VIRGINIA DEM ADMITS SYSTEM ‘FAILURE’ AFTER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED IN LANDLORD KILLING ESCAPES TO TAJIKISTAN

ICE officers transport illegal immigrants to a processing facility in Los Angeles (Fox News Digital/Peter Pinedo)

"We're out doing our job; we are sworn law enforcement officers. We're out trying to keep the community safe just like other law enforcement officers," he said. "I just think there's a lot of rhetoric out there that a lot of people don't know exactly what we do and we're trying to portray that out to the public."

Fox News Digital witnessed ICE process Aroca-Rodriguez and was told he would remain in custody pending removal to Honduras. Five other illegal immigrants were also processed for removal proceedings during the operation.

Peter Pinedo is a politics writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Prince Harry quits board of wildlife charity after rangers’ human rights abuses
articles.excerpt:
Spokesperson for Duke of Sussex says he remains an ‘active and avid supporter’ of African Parks’ mission

The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of a major African wildlife charity that ha...
articles.body_text:
Spokesperson for Duke of Sussex says he remains an ‘active and avid supporter’ of African Parks’ mission

The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of a major African wildlife charity that had been at the centre of a human rights controversy.

Prince Harry’s spokesperson confirmed he was no longer a trustee of African Parks, which admitted last year that human rights abuses were committed by its rangers in the Republic of the Congo.

The charity’s admission followed an independent review into allegations made by members of the Baka community.

In a 2024 report published by the Mail on Sunday newspaper, community members accused African Parks rangers of beating, waterboarding and raping locals to stop them from accessing their ancestral forests, which are now in a conservation area.

After the review, African Parks published a statement acknowledging that human rights abuses occurred in the Odzala-Kokoua national park, which it manages. It said that it had improved its safeguarding processes both at the park and institutionally.

A spokesperson for Harry said the duke, who was president of the charity for six years before he became a member of its board of directors in 2023, remained an active and avid supporter of African Parks.

“The duke is proud of his 10 years with African Parks and fully supports the ongoing strengthening of its board,” the spokesperson said.

“His commitment to conservation in Africa continues, and he remains a supporter of African Parks’ mission.”

Survival International, a global human rights charity that campaigns for the rights of Indigenous people, had called on Harry to step down as a member of the board.

Founded 26 years ago, African Parks manages more than 20m hectares (50m acres) in partnership with 13 African governments and hundreds of local communities.

African Parks expressed “deep gratitude” to the duke on concluding his tenure after his 10-year commitment to the organisation.

“His relationship with the organisation dates back to Malawi in July 2016, when he supported one of the largest elephant translocations in history. He served as president for six years before being appointed a member of the board of directors,” it said.

“Over the years, the duke has brought global attention to the urgent need for biodiversity protection for the benefit of people and wildlife, and has contributed greatly to promoting philanthropy for the cause of conservation in Africa. The duke remains deeply committed to this cause, and remains a strong supporter of African Parks’ work.”

The announcement comes as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are due to relocate to the UK from California with their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.

Former Suits star Meghan is said to be pursuing an acting role, with reports she has been in talks about a role in the third series of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix hit The Gentlemen, swiftly followed by other reports that the deal was off.

The couple are understood to be planning an “extended stay” in the UK, and their children are already enrolled in school, but it has not been confirmed for how long.

articles.title: Outrage in Nepal over rape and murder of three-year-old girl
articles.excerpt:
Protesters hold a banner showing the face of the child who was killed

Activists and politicians in Nepal have urged the government to enact tougher laws as the alleged rape and murder of a three-year...
articles.body_text:
Protesters hold a banner showing the face of the child who was killed

Activists and politicians in Nepal have urged the government to enact tougher laws as the alleged rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has caused outrage across the country.

Nepal has seen continued protests since the girl was found dead last week, three days after she went missing in Madhesh province.

Nine people have been arrested in connection with the case, a local police spokesman told the BBC.

The crime has triggered demands for reform. Police have also been accused of negligence in the initial stages of the investigation after footage of a teenage suspect was leaked onto social media.

After days of demonstrations in the city of Simara, the victim's family met government ministers, and secured a written agreement over the weekend.

The government has promised to review laws on serious offences, and create a memorial in honour of the child.

The incident has also opened a wider debate over how Nepal deals with young offenders, with some campaigners pushing for harsher punishments for minors convicted of rape or murder.

Prominent human rights activist Gauri Pradhan called the attack a "very painful incident and the government should punish anyone involved in such atrocious act. There should be some serious efforts for wider reforms".

However, he cautioned against calls for the introduction of the death penalty.

There has also been anger after a video showing a teenage suspect giving a statement about the suspected murder was uploaded to social media, sparking questions as to how footage recorded during a police investigation was leaked.

"We have so far found one police personnel directly involved in the [leak] and have initiated action against him," chief district officer of Bara district, Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, told the BBC.

"If more officers are found, they will also be punished. We have zero tolerance against such practice."

More than 25,500 accusations of rape and sexual abuse were filed between July 2017 to July 2025, according to Nepalese Police.

Of these cases, more than 3,200 female victims were under the age of 10, the police say.

articles.title: Vuelta a España: giant hail forces stage three abandonment in Pyrenees

Huge hailstones prompt organisers to act 15km from end

Riders seen heading into hotel on route to take cover

A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the ⁠third stage ...
articles.body_text:
Huge hailstones prompt organisers to act 15km from end

Riders seen heading into hotel on route to take cover

A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the ⁠third stage of the Vuelta a España on Monday.

With 15 kilometres (9.32 miles) remaining of the 174km route ⁠from Gruissan to Font-Romeu, the ​skies darkened as the peloton neared the top of the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began ⁠bouncing off the tarmac and pelting the riders.

Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) and Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) were 25 seconds ahead ⁠of the peloton when the elements intervened as the race leader and favourite ​Tadej Pogacar was seen indicating ‌to the peloton ‌to pull off the course.

Bedraggled riders were then seen getting off their ‌bikes and shuffling into a hotel for shelter, leaving fans frustrated at the finish where thick layers of hail blanketed the road.

“For the security of the riders, stage three has been cancelled due to hail and severe weather,” race organisers said shortly afterwards. “There will be no winner and no podium ceremony.”

Pogacar (UAE Emirates-XRG) retained his overall lead of nine seconds from the Belgian rider ‌Wout van Aert (Dutch Visma-Lease a Bike) with the British rider Matt Brennan 10sec back.

Earlier it had been warm and sunny ​on the flat approaches to the mountainous finish with no sign of the chaos to come as a five-man breakaway group stayed out ahead.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

Pogacar, bidding to complete his Grand Tour collection by winning the Vuelta ⁠for the first time, was always near the front of ​the pack with ​the Slovenian’s team setting the pace.

His expected challenge for the stage victory fell foul ​of the ‌weather in an ​anticlimactic finish. Pogacar ​will get his chance to underline his superiority again on Tuesday, though, with stage four featuring three first-category climbs as the race starts and finishes in Andorra la Vella.

articles.title: Japanese delegation seeks to soothe strained ties with China
articles.excerpt:
Japanese lawmakers have travelled to Beijing in a bid to soothe strained relations between the two nations.

The delegation landed in China on Monday for talks aimed at restoring communication. The mi...
articles.body_text:
Japanese lawmakers have travelled to Beijing in a bid to soothe strained relations between the two nations.

The delegation landed in China on Monday for talks aimed at restoring communication. The mission was undertaken after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi issued comments on Taiwan that triggered a diplomatic dispute that has begun to weigh on economic relations.

The visit will run through Thursday and marks the first such consultations with senior Chinese Communist Party officials since ties soured late last year.

Relations plunged after Takaichi suggested in November that Japan could respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan, a self-governing island that Beijing claims as its own territory.

China is highly sensitive regarding Taiwan and considers questioning of its claim on the island a red line. In response to Takaichi’s comments, it warned its citizens against travel to Japan and tightened trade restrictions, including measures that reportedly disrupted the flow of rare earth minerals to Japanese firms, adding an economic sting to the diplomatic fallout.

Among those making the trip was Gaku Hashimoto, a member of the House of Representatives and Takaichi’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party. He was joined by other lawmakers from the opposition Komeito and Centrist Reform Alliance parties.

An official from Hashimoto’s office confirmed only that he had “departed for Beijing to stay for two days”.

Before leaving Tokyo, delegation member Shinichi Isa, a spokesperson for the Centrist Reform Alliance, told reporters: “Communication has been severed in all areas, and we are beginning to see their impact in many areas. I hope we can somehow find a clue to restart a dialogue.”

Isa, a former diplomat at the Japanese embassy in China, had already sounded the alarm over the situation this month in a post on X, writing that officials had always managed to stay in contact even during past low points but now “all channels between officials and ministries have been cut off.”

He described the current state of relations as the worst since diplomatic ties were normalised in 1972.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Friday that “some people of insight from both Japan’s ruling and opposition parties” were troubled by the state of relations and hoped to help steer them back on track while calling on Tokyo to heed those voices and act to restore normal exchanges between the two countries.

Takaichi has not retracted her comment on Taiwan and is yet to respond to the concerns.

Further exchanges are planned. Former Japanese Foreign Minister Takeshi Iwaya is expected to lead another delegation to China in late September, which is to be followed by a group of Japanese business representatives later in the year, according to the Kyodo News agency.

articles.title: Iran-linked hackers suspected in UK power-plant shutdown after alleged Minnesota water attack
articles.excerpt: Former top Pentagon official and Heritage Foundation visiting fellow Steve Bucci joins 'Fox & Friends First' to analyze the surge of cyberattacks on U.S. water infrastructure. Bucci warns that state-s...
articles.body_text:
Former top Pentagon official and Heritage Foundation visiting fellow Steve Bucci joins 'Fox & Friends First' to analyze the surge of cyberattacks on U.S. water infrastructure. Bucci warns that state-sponsored actors, including Iran-backed hackers, are exploiting vulnerable digital systems in municipal utilities. He emphasizes the urgent need for local governments to isolate critical controls from the public internet.

Iran-linked hackers are suspected of forcing a small British power generator offline for four days last month, the latest sign that Tehran-linked cyber activity may be moving from probing vulnerable systems to causing disruptions U.S. officials have long warned about.

Iran-linked hackers were behind the outage, according to British security officials who spoke with multiple news outlets.

"To be clear: there was no threat to the wider grid and nobody lost power. We have one of the most resilient energy systems in the world," UK Energy Minister Michael Shanks said in a statement.

He described the generator as "tiny" but said his department had briefed CEOs following the intrusion on "steps they should take to stay secure."

The British shutdown came weeks after hackers struck more than 30 community water systems in Minnesota, accessing technology used to remotely monitor and control pumps and other equipment. Minnesota officials have not publicly attributed the attacks. Several news outlets, citing U.S. officials and a leaked industry threat-sharing memo, reported that Iran was the likely culprit. President Donald Trump has publicly rejected that assessment, saying he did not believe Iran was to blame.

Together, the incidents are putting civilian infrastructure at the center of another front in the conflict between the U.S. and Iran. As the military confrontation stretches into its sixth month, relatively small and often lightly defended water and energy facilities offer hackers a way to cause physical disruption without penetrating a major power grid or striking a military target.

Those facilities can be especially vulnerable because many rely on internet-connected industrial control systems that allow operators to monitor and manage physical equipment remotely. Once inside, hackers can interrupt operations, lock out operators or manipulate controls for pumps and other machinery.

In a July alert, the FBI and Environmental Protection Agency said malicious actors had targeted water and wastewater utilities in at least seven states by accessing exposed programmable logic controllers and changing their internet addresses and passwords. Some incidents disrupted water operations, causing reported pressure loss and flooding.

Federal agencies have also warned that Iranian-affiliated actors have targeted similar industrial devices across water, energy and government sectors, seeking access to the software used to control them. That activity has already caused operational disruptions and financial losses.

IRAN’S PROXY WAR HAS CROSSED OCEANS AND IS NOW KNOCKING ON AMERICA’S DOOR

Hackers targeted computerized controls at more than 30 Minnesota water systems, forcing some utilities to use manual operations and backup procedures. (Tony Webster/Wikimedia Commons)

Iranian hackers have pursued U.S. infrastructure before.

The threat extends beyond industrial systems. On Aug. 18, the Justice Department charged 17 members of an Iran-based company with carrying out a sweeping cyber theft campaign targeting hundreds of universities, private companies and government agencies. Prosecutors said many of the intrusions were conducted on behalf of the IRGC and other Iranian entities and resulted in the theft of more than 31 terabytes of academic data and intellectual property.

In 2016, the Justice Department charged an Iranian hacker with gaining access to the control system for a dam in Rye, New York. The dam’s sluice gate had been disconnected for maintenance at the time, preventing him from manipulating water levels and flow rates.

More recently, U.S. agencies linked an IRGC-affiliated campaign known as CyberAv3ngers to compromises of Israeli-made industrial controllers at dozens of U.S. facilities in late 2023 and early 2024, including water and wastewater systems, energy companies, food manufacturers and health care organizations. The campaign exploited devices exposed to the public internet that were still using default passwords.

The more recent attacks underscore how little access may be required to produce a physical effect. In Minnesota, compromised controllers affected systems used to track water levels, pressure, pump operations and equipment alarms; in some communities, equipment was temporarily taken offline while operators restored systems.

Whether Tehran intends a wider campaign against Western infrastructure remains unclear. But the four-day shutdown in Britain illustrates what hackers can do once they gain access to a small industrial system: disrupt physical operations without breaching a major grid operator or triggering a blackout large enough to invite an immediate military response.

articles.title: Phillies vs Mariners player props and over under picks as Philadelphia eyes 10th consecutive win
articles.excerpt:
Alanna Rizzo shares her thoughts on the MLB post-season.

Baseball tends to be a season full of streaks from teams. Some months, teams are awesome; some months they stink. It is easier to notice the s...
articles.body_text:
Alanna Rizzo shares her thoughts on the MLB post-season.

Baseball tends to be a season full of streaks from teams. Some months, teams are awesome; some months they stink. It is easier to notice the successes or failures of teams when they are earlier in the season. You can see when a team is struggling more easily when their record is 11-16 as opposed to 55-59, for example. What happens when one of the hottest teams in baseball takes on one of the coldest teams? That's what we have tonight as the Phillies play the Mariners.

The Philadelphia Phillies are one of the hottest teams in baseball, having won their ninth straight game yesterday on a walk-off homer. It was a bit of a miraculous comeback as the Phillies were down 4-0 before the team scored six in the bottom of the ninth to win it. The team has won 16 of their past 21 games and is now threatening to take over the Braves for the best team in the National League East. It is fairly unlikely that they would miss the postseason, but that wasn't something that could be said before this stretch. On July 31, they were just four games above .500 and looking like the team that started the season instead of the one that had a great turnaround.

Philadelphia Phillies starting pitcher Zack Wheeler throws against the St. Louis Cardinals during the first inning at Busch Stadium in St. Louis, Mo., on Aug. 12, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Today the team sends out one of their aces, giving them a good chance to make it to 10 wins in a row as Zack Wheeler takes the hill. Wheeler takes the ball today with a 10-4 record, 2.92 ERA, and a 1.01 WHIP. He has also racked up 144 strikeouts. He has been solid on the road this campaign with a slightly lower ERA at 2.67. This has been the worst month of his season, though. In August, he has allowed 10 earned runs over 17.1 innings of work. He hasn't completed six innings in any of his last five outings. Wheeler has been good against the Mariners in the past, holding them to a .172 batting average.

PHILLIES SEND CY YOUNG CONTENDER CHRISTOPHER SANCHEZ TO THE MOUND IN WILD CARD RACE SHOWDOWN

The Seattle Mariners are one of the most frustrating teams in baseball. They are seven games under .500 this season, despite looking like one of the best teams in baseball, at least on paper. Somehow, the team is under .500 and in jeopardy of missing the postseason. They are currently three games behind the Rangers and Astros, who are currently tied for first. It doesn't help that they also have to battle the Orioles, Twins, Blue Jays, and Guardians for the final Wild Card spot. They are also three games back in that race, and the Tigers are just behind at 3.5 games.

Seattle Mariners pitcher Logan Gilbert (36) delivers a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers in the first inning at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wis., on Aug. 19, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Looking to battle the Phillies and Wheeler is Logan Gilbert. For the season, Gilbert is 10-7 with a 3.35 ERA and a 1.01 WHIP. The problem that Gilbert has is that he has pitched much worse at home this season than on the road. He has allowed 20 homers this season, and 18 of them have come in Seattle. His road ERA is a stellar 2.49, but his home ERA is all the way up there at 4.01. He doesn't give up too many runs in the majority of starts, but this is not a place you'd want to trust him.

One guy that stands out for us to fade tonight is Randy Arozarena of the Mariners. For his career, he is just 1-for-13 against Wheeler with seven strikeouts. articles.title: Trump administration announces ‘economic D-day’ sanctions on Iran
articles.excerpt:
US Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent has announced an economic pressure campaign against Iran, vowing to target Tehran’s financial interests across the world.

Bessent said on Monday that the US wou...
articles.body_text:
US Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent has announced an economic pressure campaign against Iran, vowing to target Tehran’s financial interests across the world.

Bessent said on Monday that the US would target all of Iran’s sources of revenue, including oil, with the aim of preventing other countries and companies from doing business with Tehran.

“Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” he said.

Bessent warned what he called Iran’s facilitators to cease buying oil and trading with Tehran.

He said countries around the world must choose between the US and Iran, stressing that the new campaign exposes Tehran’s trade partners to secondary penalties.

Bessent emphasised that “no one is above the reach of US sanctions”.

If countries and entities “facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted”, he said.

The campaign is dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”. Bessent also called it “economic D-day”, likening it to the Allies’ forces landing on French shores to push back against Nazi Germany during World War II.

The economic pressure campaign comes nearly six months into the war with Iran after the US and Israel launched strikes against the country without direct provocation.

While US and Israeli attacks have killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and several other top officials, they have failed to dislodge the governing system in Tehran.

Tehran has responded to the US and Israeli strikes with missile and drone attacks across the region. It has also largely shut down and asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz, a major artery for global energy, sending oil and gas prices soaring.

Multiple rounds of fighting and diplomacy have failed to resolve the crisis.

Monday’s sanctions push is the latest effort by the US to pressure Iran to make major concessions, including giving up its nuclear programme and ceasing attacks on vessels in Hormuz.

Bessent said US President Donald Trump has been making calls to world leaders “with specific requests to cease their interaction with the regime”.

“Those who stand with the United States will reap the rewards of our partnership. Those who tether themselves to the Iranian regime should expect to share in the isolation,” he said.

The US officials said new sanctions will target “five of Iran’s most vital lifelines”: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.
